instruments.name: Access Virus A
instruments.text: The first Access Virus, a virtual analogue desktop synthesiser unveiled at Musikmesse Frankfurt in February 1997.

instruments.name: Access Virus B
instruments.text: A desktop (rackable) virtual analogue module that followed the Virus A with improved converters and more polyphony, later given three oscillators plus a sub oscillator and two filters per voice.

instruments.name: Access Virus Indigo
instruments.text: A silver Virus B with a three-octave keyboard, black knobs and blue LEDs, offering 24 voices.

instruments.name: Access Virus C
instruments.text: The third generation of the Virus virtual analogue desktop synthesiser, with more polyphony and additional synthesis features.

instruments.name: Access Virus Indigo 2
instruments.text: A portable three-octave keyboard carrying the Virus C virtual analogue engine.

instruments.name: Access Virus KC
instruments.text: The keyboard version of the Virus C, sharing its virtual analogue engine.

instruments.name: Access Virus Rack XL
instruments.text: A rack-mounted version of the Virus C, sharing its virtual analogue engine.

instruments.name: Access Virus TI
instruments.text: The Virus TI (Total Integration) series of virtual analogue synthesisers, sold as the 61-key Virus TI Keyboard and the 37-key Virus TI Polar.

instruments.name: Access Virus TI Snow
instruments.text: A small desktop Virus TI using a single DSP chip, giving it about half the polyphony of the other TI models.

instruments.name: Access Virus TI2
instruments.text: A revision of the Virus TI series with faster DSP controllers, more polyphony, more effects and a slightly changed design.

instruments.name: Akai AX80
instruments.text: An eight-voice analogue polysynth with two oscillators per voice, a resonant low-pass and high-pass filter, a five-octave velocity-sensitive keyboard and 96 memories edited through LED and LCD bar displays.

instruments.name: Akai AX60
instruments.text: A six-voice, bitimbral analogue polysynth with one VCO per voice and Curtis CEM3394 voice chips, a 61-key keyboard, an arpeggiator, BBD chorus, 64 memories and inputs that put Akai sampler sounds through its voice circuits.

instruments.name: Akai AX73
instruments.text: A six-voice digitally controlled analogue polysynth with one VCO, VCF, high-pass filter and VCA per voice on Curtis CEM3394 chips, stereo chorus and a 73-note velocity-sensitive keyboard, able to process sounds from Akai samplers.

instruments.name: Akai VX90
instruments.text: The keyboardless rack version of the AX73: a six-voice digitally controlled analogue synth module with 100 patch memories and polyphonic or unison modes.

instruments.name: Akai VX600
instruments.text: A compact analogue polysynth with a three-octave keyboard and a connection jack for Akai's EWI and EVI wind controllers.

instruments.name: Akai EWI4000s
instruments.text: A wind controller with a built-in analogue-modelling synth of two oscillators with sawtooth, triangle, square and pulse waves, 2- or 4-pole filters, breath noise and reverb, delay and chorus.

instruments.name: Akai Miniak
instruments.text: A 37-key virtual analogue synth sharing the Alesis Micron's engine, with three oscillators per voice, two multimode filters, a 40-band vocoder with gooseneck microphone, a step and phrase sequencer, rhythm patterns and an arpeggiator.

instruments.name: Akai Timbre Wolf
instruments.text: A four-voice analogue synth with 25 keys whose voices can be set up as four mono synths, a four-voice unison mono synth or a polysynth, with a 32-step sequencer for each voice.

instruments.name: Alesis QuadraSynth
instruments.text: A 76-key, 64-voice, 16-part multitimbral sample-based digital synth with 16MB of PCM waveform ROM, PCMCIA expansion cards and the first ADAT optical interface on a synth; the QuadraSynth Plus revised it.

instruments.name: Alesis S4 QuadraSynth
instruments.text: The 1U rack module of the QuadraSynth: a 64-voice sample-plus-synthesis engine with 16MB of 16-bit ROM, 16-part multitimbral Mixes and ADAT optical output.

instruments.name: Alesis QS6
instruments.text: A 64-voice sample-plus-synthesis keyboard on the QuadraSynth engine with a five-octave keyboard, 8MB of sample ROM, PCMCIA expansion and no resonant filters, followed in 1996 by the 76-key QS7 and 88-key weighted QS8 with 16MB of ROM.

instruments.name: Alesis NanoSynth
instruments.text: A third-rack, 64-voice General MIDI-compatible module with the QS6's sounds and 8MB of waveform ROM, editable in full over MIDI controllers.

instruments.name: Alesis QSR
instruments.text: A 64-voice rack module with the QS8's sample-plus-synthesis engine, 16MB of ROM, two PCMCIA slots, ADAT optical output and a serial computer connection.

instruments.name: Alesis Andromeda A6
instruments.text: A 16-voice, 16-part multitimbral analogue polysynth with two VCOs and a sub-oscillator per voice, a 2-pole multimode and a 4-pole low-pass filter per voice, a 61-key velocity and aftertouch keyboard, a ribbon and a 16-step sequencer.

instruments.name: Alesis Ion
instruments.text: An eight-voice virtual analogue synth with three oscillators per voice, 17 filter types and 49 keys.

instruments.name: Alesis Micron
instruments.text: A 37-key virtual analogue synth with almost the same engine as the Ion, whose patches it shares, adding reverb and long delay.

instruments.name: Alesis Fusion
instruments.text: A hard-disk workstation combining sample playback, virtual analogue, FM and physical-modelling synthesis with sampling and 80 effects, sold with a 61-key (6HD) or 88-key weighted (8HD) keyboard.

instruments.name: ARP 2500
instruments.text: An analogue modular synthesiser patched with a switch matrix instead of patch cords, noted for its reliable tuning.

instruments.name: ARP Soloist
instruments.text: A preset lead synthesiser with 18 preset sounds and a touch sensor, designed to be simpler to play than a modular.

instruments.name: ARP Explorer I
instruments.text: A monophonic synthesiser intended as a bridge between the programmability of the Odyssey and the preset speed of the Pro Soloist.

instruments.name: ARP Solina String Ensemble
instruments.text: A 49-note preset polyphonic string ensemble keyboard with string and brass sounds.

instruments.name: ARP Axxe
instruments.text: A lower-priced monophonic synthesiser with one VCO, one VCF, an LFO, noise, sample and hold and an ADSR envelope.

instruments.name: ARP Little Brother
instruments.text: A keyboardless expander module adding an extra VCO to synthesisers such as the Axxe and Odyssey.

instruments.name: ARP Omni
instruments.text: A fully polyphonic string synthesiser using top-octave divide-down oscillators of the kind found in electronic organs.

instruments.name: ARP Omni-2
instruments.text: An updated Omni combining a string section with a polyphonic synthesiser section.

instruments.name: ARP Pro/DGX
instruments.text: A preset monophonic synthesiser with 30 presets selected by digitally latched pushbuttons and aftertouch, the successor to the Pro Soloist.

instruments.name: ARP Quadra
instruments.text: A microprocessor-controlled instrument combining bass, string, polyphonic synth and lead sections, with 16 memories and a split 61-note keyboard.

instruments.name: ARP Quartet
instruments.text: A 49-note polyphonic keyboard with string, brass, organ and piano sounds.

instruments.name: ARP Solus
instruments.text: An affordable 37-note monophonic two-oscillator synthesiser built into its own road case, ARP's last shipping product.

instruments.name: Arturia Origin
instruments.text: Arturia's first hardware synth, a standalone DSP-based system using the same software engine as its virtual synth products.

instruments.name: Arturia MiniBrute
instruments.text: A 25-key monophonic analogue synthesiser with one voltage-controlled oscillator, two LFOs and a multimode Steiner-Parker filter.

instruments.name: Arturia MicroBrute
instruments.text: A smaller and cheaper version of the MiniBrute with mini keys, a patch bank and a sequencer.

instruments.name: Arturia MatrixBrute
instruments.text: An all-analogue monosynth with three Brute oscillators, a Steiner-Parker and a ladder filter, five analogue effects, a modulation matrix, a step sequencer and a 49-note keyboard with aftertouch.

instruments.name: Arturia MiniBrute 2
instruments.text: A semi-modular analogue monosynth with a patch bay that connects to Eurorack modular gear.

instruments.name: Arturia MiniBrute 2S
instruments.text: A semi-modular version of the MiniBrute 2 that replaces the 25-note keyboard with performance pads and a triple-layer sequencer storing up to 64 sequences.

instruments.name: Arturia MicroFreak
instruments.text: A four-voice paraphonic hybrid synthesiser with digital oscillators, an analogue filter and a touch-capacitive keyboard.

instruments.name: Arturia PolyBrute
instruments.text: A six-voice analogue polysynth, Arturia's flagship, with a layout like the MatrixBrute's and a voice architecture shared with the Brute range.

instruments.name: Arturia MiniFreak
instruments.text: A follow-up to the MicroFreak with six voices of polyphony, more functions and a larger conventional keyboard.

instruments.name: Arturia PolyBrute 12
instruments.text: A 12-voice analogue polysynth with two VCOs per voice, Steiner-Parker and ladder filters, and a 61-key FullTouch keyboard with polyphonic aftertouch.

instruments.name: Ashun Sound Machines Hydrasynth
instruments.text: An eight-voice digital wave-morphing synthesizer with three oscillators per voice, a four-octave polyphonic-aftertouch keyboard and a ribbon controller, also sold as a desktop version with the same engine.

instruments.name: Ashun Sound Machines Hydrasynth Deluxe
instruments.text: A 16-voice, bi-timbral Hydrasynth with two engines for layering and splitting, a 73-note polyphonic-aftertouch keyboard and a CV/gate section.

instruments.name: Ashun Sound Machines Hydrasynth Explorer
instruments.text: A compact eight-voice Hydrasynth with a 37-note polyphonic-aftertouch mini keyboard that can run on eight AA batteries.

instruments.name: Ashun Sound Machines Leviasynth
instruments.text: A 16-voice hybrid FM synthesizer with eight digital oscillators per voice, 144 FM algorithms, digital and analogue filters and a five-octave polyphonic-aftertouch keyboard, also made as a desktop edition with pads.

instruments.name: Behringer DeepMind 12D
instruments.text: A desktop version of the twelve-voice analogue DeepMind 12 with all of the keyboard model's features.

instruments.name: Behringer DeepMind 6
instruments.text: A six-voice analogue polysynth on a three-octave keyboard that uses the DeepMind 12's engine without that model's Wi-Fi.

instruments.name: Behringer Model D
instruments.text: A desktop analogue recreation of the Minimoog Model D with three VCOs, a 24dB ladder filter, MIDI and an external audio input, whose main module fits a Eurorack case.

instruments.name: Behringer Crave
instruments.text: A compact semi-modular synth of Behringer's own design with a patch bay and a built-in sequencer.

instruments.name: Behringer K-2
instruments.text: A keyless semi-modular recreation of the Korg MS-20 with two VCOs, ring modulation and a patch bay, in Eurorack format with polychain for up to 16 voices.

instruments.name: Behringer MS-1
instruments.text: An analogue recreation of the Roland SH-101, first named the MS-101, with one VCO, a sub-oscillator and noise, an ADSR envelope, a 2.5-octave keyboard, a 32-step sequencer, an arpeggiator and a keytar modulation grip.

instruments.name: Behringer Odyssey
instruments.text: A recreation of the ARP Odyssey in the Mark III colours with a full-size 37-key keyboard, all three of the original filter versions, MIDI, digital effects, a 32-step sequencer and an arpeggiator.

instruments.name: Behringer Pro-1
instruments.text: A desktop analogue recreation of the Sequential Circuits Pro-One: a two-oscillator Curtis-chip monosynth with a 24dB filter, two envelopes, a modulation matrix, a sequencer, an arpeggiator and CV patch points.

instruments.name: Behringer TD-3
instruments.text: An analogue recreation of the Roland TB-303 with a 4-pole low-pass filter, a 16-step pattern sequencer, a distortion circuit modelled on the Boss DS-1 and polychain for up to 16 voices.

instruments.name: Behringer Vocoder VC340
instruments.text: An analogue recreation of the Roland VP-330 Vocoder Plus that combines a vocoder with human-voice and string sections, a BBD chorus and 37 semi-weighted keys.

instruments.name: Behringer Wasp Deluxe
instruments.text: A keyless hybrid recreation of the EDP Wasp with two digital oscillators, an analogue multimode filter, two analogue envelopes with a repeat function and a control oscillator for modulation.

instruments.name: Behringer 2600
instruments.text: A recreation of the ARP 2600 in an 8U rack chassis without speakers, with a digital spring-reverb simulation, a switch between both original filter versions and sync of VCOs 2 and 3 to VCO 1.

instruments.name: Behringer CAT
instruments.text: A keyless duophonic analogue recreation of the Octave Cat with two syncable VCOs, a 24dB low-pass filter, AR and ADSR envelopes and a small patch bay, in a Eurorack-compatible case.

instruments.name: Behringer MonoPoly
instruments.text: A smaller recreation of the Korg Mono/Poly with four VCOs in mono, unison and paraphonic modes, a 24dB filter, two analogue LFOs, an arpeggiator and a 37-note keyboard.

instruments.name: Behringer System 15
instruments.text: A Eurorack recreation of the Moog System 15: 16 modules including 921 and 921B oscillators and a 914 fixed filter bank, in a Eurorack Go case with a MIDI-to-CV converter.

instruments.name: Behringer System 35
instruments.text: A Eurorack recreation of the Moog System 35: 25 modules including five oscillators, a mixer and a fixed filter bank, in a Eurorack Go case with a MIDI-to-CV converter.

instruments.name: Behringer System 55
instruments.text: A Eurorack recreation of the Moog System 55: 38 modules including up to seven oscillators, five VCAs and the 960 sequencer, in two joined Eurorack Go cases with a MIDI-to-CV converter.

instruments.name: Behringer JT-4000 Micro
instruments.text: A pocket-size four-voice hybrid synth reproducing the Roland JP-8000's sound engine and supersaw, with two analogue-modelling oscillators per voice, analogue filters, 16 touch keys and 32 presets.

instruments.name: Behringer Kobol Expander
instruments.text: A duophonic semi-modular analogue recreation of the RSF Kobol Expander with two VCOs of seven morphing waveforms, a four-pole VCF and 32 patch points, in Eurorack format.

instruments.name: Behringer Pro VS Mini
instruments.text: A pocket-size four-voice hybrid vector synth inspired by the Sequential Prophet VS, with digital oscillators blended by a joystick, an analogue filter, a touch keyboard and a sequencer.

instruments.name: Behringer Pro-800
instruments.text: A desktop recreation of the Sequential Circuits Prophet-600 expanded to eight voices, with 16 oscillators, a 24dB low-pass filter, a two-track polyphonic sequencer, an arpeggiator and 400 program slots.

instruments.name: Behringer Solina String Ensemble
instruments.text: A string machine that follows the original Solina's circuitry, with a built-in phaser modelled on the Small Stone, external modulation inputs and MIDI.

instruments.name: Behringer UB-Xa
instruments.text: A recreation of the Oberheim OB-Xa with 16 voices of two VCOs each, a 12/24dB analogue low-pass filter per voice and 61 keys with poly aftertouch, able to split or layer two sounds.

instruments.name: Behringer Grind
instruments.text: A hybrid semi-modular synth whose 24 digital oscillator engines, 15 of them from Mutable Instruments' Plaits, feed an analogue ladder filter, with a 32-step sequencer, an arpeggiator and a 34-point patch bay.

instruments.name: Behringer JT Mini
instruments.text: A pocket-size three-voice paraphonic analogue synth inspired by the Roland Jupiter-8, with three VCOs, a 2/4-pole multimode filter, 27 touch keys, a 16-step motion sequencer and an arpeggiator.

instruments.name: Behringer Model 15
instruments.text: A desktop semi-modular analogue synth after the Moog Grandmother with two oscillators and a sub-oscillator, 48 patch points, a 256-step sequencer and arpeggiator and an emulated spring reverb.

instruments.name: Behringer MS-5
instruments.text: A reproduction of the Roland SH-5 circuit with two VCOs, a multimode VCF plus a separate band-pass filter, a ring modulator, two analogue LFOs, sample and hold, and 37 keys in a folding case.

instruments.name: Behringer Phara-O Mini
instruments.text: A pocket-size paraphonic analogue synth with three VCOs, a low-pass filter based on the Korg miniKORG 700S, a ring modulator, a delay, 27 touch keys and a 16-step motion sequencer.

instruments.name: Behringer Proton
instruments.text: A paraphonic analogue semi-modular synth of Behringer's own design with two VCOs, two VCFs in series or parallel, four envelopes, a wave folder and 64 patch points.

instruments.name: Behringer Spice
instruments.text: A desktop semi-modular analogue synth after the Moog Subharmonicon, with two oscillators, four sub-oscillators, a ladder filter and two four-step polyrhythmic sequencers, patched through a 16 x 16 matrix.

instruments.name: Behringer UB-Xa D
instruments.text: A 16-voice desktop and rack version of the UB-Xa, with VCOs and dual VCFs based on the 3340 and 3320 chip designs of the Oberheim OB-Xa and 512 program memories.

instruments.name: Behringer Wave
instruments.text: A recreation of the PPG Wave 2.2 and 2.3: an eight-voice multitimbral hybrid wavetable synth with 16 digital oscillators, a 24dB analogue low-pass filter and 49 keys with aftertouch.

instruments.name: Behringer 2-XM
instruments.text: A keyless Eurorack-format recreation of the Oberheim Two Voice with two independent voices, each with a multimode low-pass, high-pass, band-pass and notch filter, played polyphonic, split or in unison over MIDI and USB.

instruments.name: Behringer CZ-1 Mini
instruments.text: A pocket-size three-voice hybrid synth after the Casio CZ series, with phase-distortion oscillators into an analogue low-pass filter, 27 touch keys, a 16-step sequencer, an arpeggiator and chorus.

instruments.name: Behringer UB-1 Micro
instruments.text: A pocket-size analogue monosynth drawing on the circuits of the Oberheim Matrix-6 and Matrix-1000, with two DCOs, a sub-oscillator, a 24dB low-pass VCF, 16 touch keys and an arpeggiator.

instruments.name: Behringer UB-Xa Mini
instruments.text: A pocket-size three-voice paraphonic analogue synth with three VCOs and a 12/24dB low-pass filter using reproduced OB-Xa circuitry, and a 16-step motion sequencer.

instruments.name: Behringer D Mini
instruments.text: A pocket-size three-voice paraphonic analogue synth based on the Minimoog, with three oscillators, a ladder low-pass filter, 27 touch keys and a 16-step sequencer.

instruments.name: Behringer JN-80
instruments.text: A recreation of the Roland Juno-60 expanded to eight voices, with a discrete DCO per voice, a 24dB low-pass filter based on 3109 circuitry, a BBD chorus, an arpeggiator and 49 keys with poly aftertouch.

instruments.name: Behringer JT-2
instruments.text: A keyless Eurorack-format analogue synth reproducing a single Roland Jupiter-8 voice, with two oscillators played paraphonically, a 12/24dB low-pass and a high-pass filter, two ADSRs, an arpeggiator and polychain.

instruments.name: Black Corporation Deckard's Dream
instruments.text: An eight-voice analogue polysynth modelled on the Yamaha CS-80, with two layers per voice, 16 VCOs, polyphonic aftertouch and MPE, sold built or as a DIY kit.

instruments.name: Black Corporation Kijimi
instruments.text: An eight-voice analogue polysynth in a 4U rack-style case with two oscillators per voice and a 24dB low-pass filter, inspired by the RSF PolyKobol II without being a copy of it.

instruments.name: Buchla 400
instruments.text: A self-contained, microprocessor-controlled six-voice multi-timbral instrument with a 12 dB resonant lowpass filter per voice and a graphical interface on a colour video display; close to forty were sold.

instruments.name: Buchla 700
instruments.text: A fully MIDI-equipped hybrid with digital sound generation influenced by FM and analogue filters and amplifiers, played from a touch-plate keyboard; very few were sold.

instruments.name: Buchla 200e Skylab
instruments.text: A portable 200e modular system of twelve modules in a powered cabinet, including waveform generators, filters and a sequential voltage source, with patch storage.

instruments.name: Buchla Music Easel (2013)
instruments.text: The Music Easel re-introduced by BEMI a year after it took over Buchla & Associates in 2012.

instruments.name: Buchla Easel Command
instruments.text: The Music Easel's 208C sound source in a standalone desktop case with MIDI, adding five audio inputs and outputs and five CV inputs for the modulation and complex oscillators, envelope and gate.

instruments.name: Casio CZ-1000
instruments.text: A digital phase-distortion synth functionally identical to the CZ-101, with four voices from eight oscillators, but with a 49-key full-size keyboard.

instruments.name: Casio CZ-101
instruments.text: A battery-powered digital phase-distortion synth with 49 mini keys and eight oscillators giving four voices (eight with one oscillator per voice), with eight-stage envelopes, and the first fully programmable synth sold for under $500.

instruments.name: Casio CZ-5000
instruments.text: A digital phase-distortion synth with a five-octave keyboard without velocity, eight voices from 16 oscillators, eight digital waveforms, stereo chorus and an eight-track real- and step-time sequencer.

instruments.name: Casio CZ-1
instruments.text: The top CZ phase-distortion synth, with two DCOs, DCWs and DCAs per voice, a five-octave keyboard with velocity and aftertouch, split and dual modes, a backlit display and 64 preset and 64 user memories.

instruments.name: Casio CZ-230S
instruments.text: A phase-distortion CZ synth with 49 mini keys, 100 preset tones with limited programmability and a built-in drum machine using RZ-1 sounds.

instruments.name: Casio CZ-3000
instruments.text: A digital phase-distortion synth with a 61-key keyboard, eight voices from 16 oscillators, keyboard split and layer, a stereo chorus and pitch and mod wheels: the CZ-5000 without its sequencer.

instruments.name: Casio FZ-1
instruments.text: A 16-bit eight-voice sampling keyboard with 1MB of memory expandable to 2MB, a five-octave velocity- and aftertouch-sensitive keyboard, a graphic display for waveform editing, digital wave synthesis and eight individual outputs.

instruments.name: Casio HZ-600
instruments.text: A 61-key, eight-voice splittable digital synth using Casio's SD synthesis, a simplified variant of phase distortion, and the only SD model built like a professional synth, without speakers or auto-accompaniment.

instruments.name: Casio VZ-1
instruments.text: A 16-voice digital keyboard synth using Casio's iPD (interactive phase distortion) synthesis, with eight configurable sound modules per voice and a multitimbral mode.

instruments.name: Casio VZ-10M
instruments.text: The rack-mount version of the VZ-1: a 16-voice multitimbral iPD (interactive phase distortion) digital synth module.

instruments.name: Casio VZ-8M
instruments.text: A 1U rack iPD (interactive phase distortion) expander with eight voices, an eight-part Multi mode and a 2x16-character display, the cheapest of the VZ range.

instruments.name: Casio XW-G1
instruments.text: A 61-key groove synth with 420 preset tones including Solo Synthesizer and PCM tones, a step sequencer, a phrase sequencer and a sample looper of up to 19 seconds for DJ-style performance.

instruments.name: Casio XW-P1
instruments.text: A 61-key battery-capable performance synth with 620 preset tones, including Solo Synthesizer presets of analogue-style sounds, six-tone Hex Layer presets and drawbar organ, more than 2,100 PCM waves, step and phrase sequencers and four-zone performance setups.

instruments.name: Cheetah MS6
instruments.text: A 1U rack expander with six voices, six-part multitimbrality and 12 DCOs.

instruments.name: Cheetah MS800
instruments.text: A 15-note polyphonic, multitimbral digital wave-sequencing synthesiser module with no filter.

instruments.name: Nord Lead
instruments.text: Clavia's first synthesiser, a 49-key virtual analogue subtractive instrument with four voices expandable to twelve, known for popularising the term virtual analogue, and also sold as the Nord Rack.

instruments.name: Nord Lead 2
instruments.text: A 49-key virtual analogue subtractive synthesiser that raised the Nord Lead's polyphony from four to sixteen voices, also sold as the Nord Rack 2.

instruments.name: Nord Modular
instruments.text: A digital modular synthesiser patched from a computer editor, with four DSPs (expandable to eight) running up to 32 voices, sold as a keyboard and as a rack, and described by Nord as the first digital modular synthesiser.

instruments.name: Nord Micro Modular
instruments.text: A small four-knob desktop version of the Nord Modular, patched from the same computer software but with less DSP power, up to four voices and no multitimbrality.

instruments.name: Nord Lead 3
instruments.text: A 24-voice, 49-key virtual analogue subtractive synthesiser that added four-operator FM (sine modulation) synthesis, also sold as the Nord Rack 3.

instruments.name: Nord Lead 2X
instruments.text: A 20-voice update of the Nord Lead 2, a 49-key virtual analogue subtractive synthesiser, also sold as the Nord Rack 2X.

instruments.name: Nord Modular G2
instruments.text: The second-generation Nord Modular, a digital modular synthesiser whose patches are built in software, also sold as the G2X.

instruments.name: Nord Wave
instruments.text: A performance synthesiser and sampler that, in Nord's words, took the Nord Lead concept to a new level.

instruments.name: Nord Lead 4
instruments.text: A 20-voice, 49-key virtual analogue subtractive synthesiser with an updated engine and an effects section.

instruments.name: Nord Lead A1
instruments.text: A 26-voice, 49-key virtual analogue subtractive synthesiser.

instruments.name: Nord Wave 2
instruments.text: A four-part, 48-voice performance synthesiser combining virtual analogue, sample, FM and wavetable synthesis, with 1 GB of sample memory and a 61-note keyboard with aftertouch.

instruments.name: Clef Microsynth
instruments.text: A two-VCO, one-VCF monophonic synthesiser with a 30-note keyboard and noise generator.

instruments.name: Cre8audio East Beast
instruments.text: A small East Coast-style analogue semi-modular made with Pittsburgh Modular, with a Pittsburgh multimode filter, a button keyboard, a 32-step sequencer and MIDI, removable as a 40hp Eurorack module.

instruments.name: Cre8audio West Pest
instruments.text: A small West Coast-style monophonic semi-modular made with Pittsburgh Modular, with wavefolding, a Dynamics Controller, a digital multi-mod tool, a sequencer and 18 Eurorack patch points.

instruments.name: Crumar Stringman
instruments.text: A 61-note string synthesiser with violin, cello and bass sounds and a three-band EQ.

instruments.name: Crumar Multiman
instruments.text: A 61-note string, brass and piano keyboard, later revised as the Multiman S3.

instruments.name: Crumar DS-1
instruments.text: A monophonic synthesiser with two digitally controlled oscillators and a 44-note keyboard.

instruments.name: Crumar DS-2
instruments.text: A two-DCO monophonic synthesiser with a 44-note keyboard and an added string section.

instruments.name: Crumar Performer
instruments.text: A 49-note polyphonic string and brass synthesiser.

instruments.name: Crumar Trilogy
instruments.text: A 49-note polyphonic string and organ synthesiser with two oscillators, seven presets and joystick control.

instruments.name: Crumar Composer
instruments.text: A 49-note keyboard combining string and brass sections with a polyphonic and monophonic synthesiser.

instruments.name: Crumar Stratus
instruments.text: A 49-note polyphonic string, brass and organ synthesiser with two oscillators, invertible envelopes and joystick control.

instruments.name: Crumar Synthephone
instruments.text: A 37-note monophonic synthesiser played with a breath controller for expression.

instruments.name: Crumar Spirit
instruments.text: A two-VCO monophonic synthesiser with a 37-note keyboard, ring modulation, switchable 12dB and 24dB filters and three modulation wheels.

instruments.name: Crumar Bit One
instruments.text: A 61-note velocity-sensitive polysynth with 12 DCOs, sold under Crumar's Bit brand.

instruments.name: Crumar Bit 01
instruments.text: A six-voice, 12-DCO expander module version of the Bit polysynths.

instruments.name: Crumar Bit 99
instruments.text: A 61-note velocity-sensitive polysynth with 12 DCOs that followed the Bit One under Crumar's Bit brand.

instruments.name: Dave Smith Instruments Evolver
instruments.text: A monophonic desktop hybrid synthesiser with two analogue and two digital wavetable oscillators, an analogue low-pass filter, a digital high-pass filter and a 4x16 step sequencer.

instruments.name: Dave Smith Instruments Poly Evolver
instruments.text: A four-voice polyphonic version of the Evolver's analogue-digital hybrid engine, first sold as a rack unit and from 2005 as a 61-key keyboard.

instruments.name: Dave Smith Instruments Mono Evolver Keyboard
instruments.text: A 37-key keyboard version of the monophonic Evolver, with two analogue and two digital wavetable oscillators, a Curtis filter per channel and an arpeggiator.

instruments.name: Dave Smith Instruments Mopho
instruments.text: A compact monophonic desktop synthesiser with an all-analogue signal path, two oscillators, two sub-octave generators, a switchable 2- or 4-pole Curtis low-pass filter and a 16x4 step sequencer.

instruments.name: Dave Smith Instruments Tetra
instruments.text: A four-voice, four-part multitimbral analogue desktop synthesiser built as four Mopho voices in one box, with an individual output per voice.

instruments.name: Dave Smith Instruments Mopho x4
instruments.text: A four-voice analogue polysynth on the Mopho voice architecture, with two oscillators and a Curtis low-pass filter per voice and a 44-note semi-weighted keyboard.

instruments.name: Dave Smith Instruments Prophet 12
instruments.text: A twelve-voice hybrid polysynth with four digital oscillators and a sub-oscillator per voice, resonant analogue low- and high-pass filters and a character section.

instruments.name: Dave Smith Instruments Pro 2
instruments.text: A monophonic hybrid keyboard synthesiser, four-voice paraphonic on demand, with four digital oscillators plus a sub-oscillator, dual analogue filters in series or parallel and a step sequencer.

instruments.name: Dave Smith Instruments OB-6
instruments.text: A six-voice analogue polysynth made with Tom Oberheim, with a sound engine based on the Oberheim SEM and a polyphonic step sequencer.

instruments.name: Dave Smith Instruments Prophet Rev2
instruments.text: A successor to the Prophet '08 with 16 voices (or 8), two DCOs and a 2- or 4-pole Curtis low-pass filter per voice, bi-timbral splits and layers, effects and a five-octave keyboard.

instruments.name: Davolisint
instruments.text: Described as the first Italian synthesiser, a monophonic two-octave instrument with a divide-down square-wave generator at seven footages, vibrato and portamento but no filter or envelope generators.

instruments.name: Dewtron Gipsy
instruments.text: A two-VCO monophonic synthesiser with a 37-note keyboard, vernier pitch knobs, ring modulator and spring reverb in a mahogany case.

instruments.name: DGS Spider
instruments.text: A three-VCO monophonic synthesiser with a 37-note keyboard and a patchbay on its sharply angled rear panel.

instruments.name: Crumar GDS
instruments.text: The General Development System, a Z80-based digital additive synthesiser with disk drives and a keyboard, made by Digital Keyboards, a collaboration of Crumar and Music Technologies of New York, and priced around $30,000.

instruments.name: Digital Keyboards Synergy
instruments.text: A lower-cost repackaging of the GDS additive synthesiser into a single case with a 77-key keyboard and no separate computer, used by Wendy Carlos.

instruments.name: Doepfer MS-404
instruments.text: A 1U rack MIDI-controlled monophonic analogue synthesizer with one VCO, a 24 dB resonant low-pass filter, an analogue ADSR and two analogue LFOs.

instruments.name: Doepfer Dark Energy
instruments.text: A standalone monophonic analogue desktop synthesizer with USB/MIDI and CV connections, a triangle-based VCO and a 24 dB low-pass filter built around the CEM3394 chip.

instruments.name: Doepfer Dark Energy II
instruments.text: A redesign of the Dark Energy after the CEM3394 went out of production, with a sawtooth-based VCO, a 12 dB multimode filter and internal pin headers for expansion.

instruments.name: Doepfer Dark Energy III
instruments.text: A monophonic analogue desktop synthesizer with a triangle-core VCO that needs no settling time, the Dark Energy II's filter, two resettable LFOs, CV inputs, MIDI and USB.

instruments.name: Dreadbox Murmux
instruments.text: Dreadbox's first synthesizer line, a handmade analogue monosynth with two VCOs with sub-octave, a four-pole resonant low-pass filter and separate filter and amp envelopes, sold in Initiate, semi-modular and pedal versions.

instruments.name: Dreadbox Erebus
instruments.text: A desktop duophonic analogue synth, sold as paraphonic, with two VCOs, a two-pole filter, a built-in digital delay and a patchbay of nine inputs and six outputs.

instruments.name: Dreadbox Hades
instruments.text: A through-hole analogue bass monosynth with one VCO and two sub-octaves, a three-pole resonant low-pass filter, OTA distortion and a small patch matrix.

instruments.name: Dreadbox Abyss
instruments.text: A four-voice analogue desktop polysynth with one oscillator and a sub-oscillator per voice, a four-pole low-pass filter and built-in BBD, delay and phaser effects.

instruments.name: Dreadbox Nyx
instruments.text: A paraphonic analogue desktop synth with two VCOs, a dual state-variable filter, a reverb by Crazy Tube Circuits and 15 patch points for re-routing.

instruments.name: Dreadbox Typhon
instruments.text: A USB-powered analogue monosynth with two VCOs and a four-pole low-pass filter under digital control, with Sinevibes stereo effects, a 32-step sequencer and 256 presets.

instruments.name: Dreadbox Nymphes
instruments.text: A USB-powered six-voice analogue polysynth with one wave-forming oscillator, sub-oscillator and noise per voice, a 24dB low-pass and a high-pass filter, a digital reverb and six playing modes.

instruments.name: Dreadbox Murmux Adept
instruments.text: An eight-voice analogue desktop polysynth limited to 300 units, with two VCOs per voice, a 24dB low-pass and 6dB high-pass filter, a BBD chorus/flanger and a hybrid stereo delay.

instruments.name: Dreadbox Artemis
instruments.text: A six-voice analogue desktop polysynth with two VCOs per voice, a sub-oscillator or noise, and an effects section made with Sinevibes.

instruments.name: Dubreq Stylophone
instruments.text: A miniature monophonic instrument played with a stylus on a 20-note keyboard, with a built-in speaker.

instruments.name: Dubreq Stylophone 350S
instruments.text: A larger monophonic Stylophone with two styli, three presets, vibrato, decay and a seven-inch speaker.

instruments.name: E-mu Emulator II
instruments.text: An eight-voice 8-bit sampling keyboard with 512 kB to 1 MB of sample memory.

instruments.name: E-mu Emax
instruments.text: A sampling keyboard, also sold as a rack, with 512 KB of sample memory and analogue filter chips, priced below the Emulator.

instruments.name: E-mu Emulator III
instruments.text: A sampling keyboard storing 16-bit, 44 kHz stereo samples in four or eight megabytes of memory, later also sold as a rack.

instruments.name: E-mu Emax II
instruments.text: A 16-bit sampling keyboard with digital filters, replacing the original Emax's analogue filter chips.

instruments.name: E-mu Proteus MPS
instruments.text: A 61-key keyboard version of the first Proteus module, the Master Performance System.

instruments.name: E-mu Proteus/1
instruments.text: A rack-mount sample-playback module with 32-voice polyphony and 192 patches, holding general sounds from the Emulator library in ROM.

instruments.name: E-mu Proteus/1 Plus Orchestral
instruments.text: A rack-mount sample-playback module combining the sounds of the first two Proteus modules.

instruments.name: E-mu Proteus/2
instruments.text: A rack-mount sample-playback module with 32-voice polyphony, specialising in orchestral sounds.

instruments.name: E-mu Proteus/3
instruments.text: A rack-mount sample-playback module with 32-voice polyphony and sounds for world music.

instruments.name: E-mu Morpheus
instruments.text: A rack-mount sample-playback module with a complex filter engine offering 197 filter presets.

instruments.name: E-mu Vintage Keys
instruments.text: The first Proteus-family module built on E-mu's new DSP chip, adding a low-pass filter to sample playback.

instruments.name: E-mu Classic Keys
instruments.text: A rack-mount sample-playback module that followed the Vintage Keys on the same filtered DSP platform.

instruments.name: E-mu Proteus FX
instruments.text: A cost-reduced, extended Proteus/1 Plus Orchestral with built-in effects and 512 presets.

instruments.name: E-mu UltraProteus
instruments.text: An extended Morpheus with the sounds of the three Proteus modules.

instruments.name: E-mu E4K
instruments.text: A 76-key weighted keyboard version of the Emulator IV sampler, expandable to 128 voices and 128 MB of memory.

instruments.name: E-mu Orbit
instruments.text: A rack-mount sample-playback module with sounds for techno and electronica.

instruments.name: E-mu Carnaval
instruments.text: A rack-mount sample-playback module with sounds for Latin music.

instruments.name: E-mu Planet Phatt
instruments.text: A rack-mount sample-playback module with sounds for hip-hop.

instruments.name: E-mu Audity 2000
instruments.text: A third-generation Proteus-family sample-playback module with electronic and dance sounds.

instruments.name: E-mu Proteus 2000
instruments.text: A rack-mount sample-playback module with up to 128 voices of polyphony and 32-part multitimbrality.

instruments.name: E-mu B-3
instruments.text: A Proteus 2000-series sample-playback module with Hammond organ sounds and Leslie emulation.

instruments.name: E-mu Mo'Phatt
instruments.text: A Proteus 2000-series sample-playback module with hip-hop sounds.

instruments.name: E-mu Planet Earth
instruments.text: A Proteus 2000-series sample-playback module with world music sounds.

instruments.name: E-mu Proteus Orchestra
instruments.text: A Proteus 2000-series sample-playback module with orchestral sounds.

instruments.name: E-mu Virtuoso 2000
instruments.text: A Proteus 2000-series sample-playback module with orchestral sounds.

instruments.name: E-mu Xtreme Lead-1
instruments.text: A Proteus 2000-series sample-playback module optimised for monophonic synthesizer solo sounds.

instruments.name: E-mu MK-6
instruments.text: An entry-level 61-key keyboard version of the Proteus 2500 module, sharing its keyboard and controls with the PK-6 and XK-6 but with its own sound set.

instruments.name: E-mu MP-7 Command Station
instruments.text: A tabletop repackaging of the Proteus sound engine with a sequencer and touch-sensitive pads for recording drum patterns, with a different sound set from the XL-7.

instruments.name: E-mu Orbit 3
instruments.text: A Proteus 2000-series sample-playback module with techno, dance and electronica sounds.

instruments.name: E-mu PK-6
instruments.text: An entry-level 61-key keyboard version of the Proteus 2500 module, sharing its keyboard and controls with the MK-6 and XK-6 but with its own sound set.

instruments.name: E-mu XK-6
instruments.text: An entry-level 61-key keyboard version of the Proteus 2500 module, sharing its keyboard and controls with the PK-6 and MK-6 but with its own sound set.

instruments.name: E-mu XL-7 Command Station
instruments.text: A tabletop repackaging of the Proteus sound engine with a sequencer and touch-sensitive pads for recording drum patterns.

instruments.name: E-mu Proteus 1000
instruments.text: A 64-voice variant of the Proteus 2000 sample-playback module.

instruments.name: E-mu Turbo Phatt
instruments.text: A Proteus 2000-series sample-playback module with hip-hop sounds.

instruments.name: E-mu Vintage Pro
instruments.text: A Proteus 2000-series sample-playback module with vintage synthesizer sounds.

instruments.name: EKO Ekosynth P15
instruments.text: A 15-preset monophonic synthesiser with a 44-note keyboard, VCF, VCA and LFO.

instruments.name: Electro-Harmonix Mini-Synthesizer
instruments.text: A one-VCO monophonic synthesiser with a 25-note touch keyboard.

instruments.name: EDP Gnat
instruments.text: A single-oscillator version of the Wasp: one digital oscillator, a resonant low-pass filter, an attack–decay envelope, an LFO and a built-in speaker, played from a 25-note touch keyboard.

instruments.name: EML Electrocomp 200
instruments.text: A monophonic two-VCO expander with no keyboard, sold to extend EML's Electrocomp systems.

instruments.name: EML Electrocomp 100
instruments.text: A duophonic portable suitcase synthesiser from EML, produced a year before the ARP 2600.

instruments.name: EML Electrocomp 101
instruments.text: A duophonic semi-modular synthesiser with four oscillators and a 44-note keyboard, built on the design of the Electrocomp 100.

instruments.name: EML Electrocomp 500
instruments.text: A two-VCO monophonic performance synthesiser with a keyboard, essentially EML's 401 sequencer-system synth in keyboard form, built to compete with the Minimoog and ARP Odyssey.

instruments.name: EML SynKey
instruments.text: A 44-note programmable synthesiser using organ-style divide-down oscillators, with its patches stored on punched cards; the SynKey 1500 was followed by the semi-programmable SynKey 2001.

instruments.name: EMS Synthi E
instruments.text: A simplified Synthi A for the schools market, with a yellow face panel, large control labels and an internal speaker, housed in a suitcase.

instruments.name: EMS PolySynthi
instruments.text: A polyphonic synthesizer with an unusual rocking keyboard mechanism and an aftertouch effect.

instruments.name: Elektron SidStation
instruments.text: Elektron's first product, a synthesiser built around the MOS Technology SID chip from the Commodore 64 home computer.

instruments.name: Elektron Monomachine
instruments.text: A six-part digital synth with five synthesis engines (SID, VO, FM+, SuperWave and DigiPro), sold as the SFX-6 keyboard with a joystick and the SFX-60 desktop module.

instruments.name: Elektron Analog Four
instruments.text: Elektron's first analogue instrument, a four-voice synth with two oscillators per voice, effects and the Elektron step sequencer with parameter locks.

instruments.name: Elektron Analog Keys
instruments.text: A four-voice analogue synthesiser with two oscillators, two sub-oscillators, dual filters and overdrive per voice, and a 37-key semi-weighted keyboard with aftertouch.

instruments.name: Elektron Digitone
instruments.text: Elektron's first FM synthesiser, with eight voices combining FM with a subtractive signal path, and four internal and four external sequencer tracks.

instruments.name: Elektron Digitone Keys
instruments.text: An eight-voice FM synth using the Digitone's engine, with a 37-note keyboard with velocity and aftertouch and four separate track outputs.

instruments.name: Elektron Digitone II
instruments.text: A 16-voice, 16-track digital synth with four synth machines (Wavetone, Swarmer, FM Tone and FM Drum), six filter types and a 128-step sequencer.

instruments.name: Elka Rhapsody 490
instruments.text: A fully polyphonic 49-key string machine with violoncello and strings sounds that can be combined.

instruments.name: Elka Rhapsody 610
instruments.text: A fully polyphonic 61-key string machine with violoncello, strings, piano and clavichord sounds and a keyboard split.

instruments.name: Elka Solist 505
instruments.text: A monophonic analogue preset synthesizer with a Moog ladder filter, 11 presets and a variation mode for attack, decay, resonance, filter frequency and vibrato.

instruments.name: Elka EK-22
instruments.text: A six-voice analogue synthesizer with two oscillators and a velocity- and pressure-sensitive keyboard with split options.

instruments.name: Elka EK-44
instruments.text: A nine-voice multitimbral FM synthesizer with a five-octave velocity- and pressure-sensitive keyboard.

instruments.name: Elka EM-22
instruments.text: The expander version of the EK-22 six-voice analogue synthesizer.

instruments.name: Elka EM-44
instruments.text: The expander version of the EK-44 nine-voice FM synthesizer.

instruments.name: Ensoniq Mirage
instruments.text: An 8-bit, 8-voice sampling keyboard with an analogue resonant four-pole low-pass filter per voice and a 61-key velocity-sensitive keyboard, known for bringing sampling within reach of many more musicians at $1,695.

instruments.name: Ensoniq ESQ-1
instruments.text: An 8-voice digital-wave synthesiser with three oscillators per voice from 32 ROM waveforms, an analogue resonant low-pass filter per voice, a 61-key velocity-sensitive keyboard and a built-in sequencer.

instruments.name: Ensoniq ESQ-M
instruments.text: A rackmount version of the ESQ-1 synthesiser without its sequencer and with a reduced display and controls.

instruments.name: Ensoniq EPS
instruments.text: The Mirage's successor, a 20-voice, 13-bit performance sampling keyboard with 61 keys, polyphonic aftertouch and a built-in sequencer.

instruments.name: Ensoniq SQ-80
instruments.text: An enhanced successor to the ESQ-1: an 8-voice synthesiser with three wavetable oscillators and an analogue filter per voice, more waveforms, a polyphonic-aftertouch keyboard, a floppy disk drive and an eight-track sequencer.

instruments.name: Ensoniq VFX
instruments.text: A 21-voice synthesiser combining Transwave wavetable synthesis, sample playback and subtractive synthesis, with a polyphonic-aftertouch keyboard.

instruments.name: Ensoniq VFX-SD
instruments.text: A version of the VFX with a 24-track sequencer, using Transwave wavetable synthesis, sample playback and subtractive synthesis with polyphonic aftertouch.

instruments.name: Ensoniq SD-1
instruments.text: A Transwave wavetable and sample-playback workstation following the VFX-SD, with dual multimode digital filters, three envelopes and an on-board sequencer, later offered with 32 voices as the SD-1/32.

instruments.name: Ensoniq SQ-1
instruments.text: A 61-key workstation with sampled and Transwave waveforms, two digital filters per voice, effects and an eight- or 16-track sequencer, later updated as the SQ-1 Plus.

instruments.name: Ensoniq SQ-R
instruments.text: A rack-mounted sound module version of the SQ-1 synthesiser.

instruments.name: Ensoniq EPS-16 Plus
instruments.text: The EPS sampling keyboard's successor, with 16-bit samples and a 24-bit effects system.

instruments.name: Ensoniq SQ-2
instruments.text: A 76-key member of Ensoniq's SQ workstation series.

instruments.name: Ensoniq ASR-10
instruments.text: A 31-voice, 16-bit sampling keyboard with 61 polyphonic-aftertouch keys, onboard effects and a 16-track sequencer, also sold with 88 weighted keys as the ASR-88 and as the rackmount ASR-10R.

instruments.name: Ensoniq KS-32
instruments.text: A 76-note weighted-action keyboard synthesiser with 32-voice polyphony, Transwave and sampled waveforms, effects and an eight-track sequencer.

instruments.name: Ensoniq TS-10
instruments.text: A 32-note polyphonic synthesiser with up to six oscillators per patch, sample playback from ROM and RAM, 24-bit effects, a sequencer and 61 polyphonic-aftertouch keys.

instruments.name: Ensoniq TS-12
instruments.text: The TS-10's synthesis and effects in a version with 76 weighted Fatar keys and channel aftertouch.

instruments.name: Ensoniq KT-76
instruments.text: A weighted-action keyboard workstation with 76 keys, also sold with 88 keys as the KT-88.

instruments.name: Ensoniq MR-61
instruments.text: A 64-voice music workstation with a 16-track sequencer, effects, several hundred onboard sounds and an Idea Pad that captures recent playing, sold with 61 keys and with 76 weighted keys as the MR-76.

instruments.name: Ensoniq Fizmo
instruments.text: A 48-voice Transwave synthesiser with two oscillators per voice, resonant digital filters, a 61-key semi-weighted keyboard and five control knobs named F-I-Z-M-O.

instruments.name: Ensoniq ZR-76
instruments.text: A 76-key Ensoniq keyboard released in 1998.

instruments.name: Ensoniq Halo
instruments.text: A 61-key sample-playback keyboard made by E-mu, a keyboard version of the Proteus 2500 module sharing the layout of the E-mu MK-6, XK-6 and PK-6 with its own soundset.

instruments.name: Erica Synths Bassline DB-01
instruments.text: A compact analogue bass synth with one VCO, a transistor sub-oscillator, a Polivoks-based two-pole filter, overdrive and a 64-step sequencer with accent and slide.

instruments.name: Erica Synths Syntrx
instruments.text: An analogue synthesizer whose interface follows the EMS Synthi AKS, with three VCOs, a resonant filter, ring modulator, spring reverb, joystick and a digitally controlled analogue patch matrix with stored patches.

instruments.name: Erica Synths Syntrx II
instruments.text: The successor to the Syntrx, with two main oscillators and a modulation oscillator, high- and low-pass filters, ring modulator, delay and reverb, a recordable joystick, a stored analogue patch matrix and a piano-roll sequencer.

instruments.name: Erica Synths Bullfrog
instruments.text: An educational analogue subtractive synth made with Richie Hawtin, with a VCO, noise, filter, VCA/delay, two envelopes and sample and hold patched together by cable or by plug-in voice cards.

instruments.name: Erica Synths Steampipe
instruments.text: An eight-voice physical-modelling desktop synth developed with 112dB, using Karplus-Strong-style feedback loops rather than oscillators to imitate wind and string instruments.

instruments.name: Expressive E Osmose
instruments.text: A 49-key polyphonic synthesizer with per-note expressive key movement, running Haken Audio's EaganMatrix engine, the same engine as the Continuum Fingerboard.

instruments.name: Fairlight CMI Series II
instruments.text: An eight-voice 8-bit sampling keyboard system sampling at up to 32 kHz, with MIDI added in the Series IIx of 1983.

instruments.name: Fairlight CMI Series III
instruments.text: A 16-voice sampling keyboard system with 16-bit, 44.1 kHz sampling and 14 MB of sample memory.

instruments.name: Farfisa Syntorchestra
instruments.text: A three-octave keyboard combining a polyphonic string ensemble with a monophonic analogue synthesiser, with separate outputs for each section.

instruments.name: Farfisa Polychrome
instruments.text: A 61-note multi-instrument keyboard with percussive, string, ensemble and vocal sections and a programmable split.

instruments.name: Farfisa Soundmaker
instruments.text: A 61-note preset keyboard developed from the Syntorchestra, with an improved string sound and a more adjustable monophonic synthesiser section with VCF, VCA, ADSR and LFO.

instruments.name: Firstman FS4V
instruments.text: A 49-note polyphonic string synthesiser with string presets, seven variable presets and a polysynth section.

instruments.name: Firstman SQ-01
instruments.text: A monophonic synthesiser with a 1024-event sequencer and a 13-note printed keypad, also sold as the Multivox SQ-01.

instruments.name: Formanta Polivoks
instruments.text: A Soviet duophonic analogue synthesiser with two oscillators, a filter switchable between low-pass and band-pass and a 48-key keyboard, of which around 32,000 were made.

instruments.name: Fuller PP2000
instruments.text: A 49-note polyphonic keyboard with one waveform at 2', 4' and 8', noise, a VCA, LFO and ADSR, and pitch bend.

instruments.name: Gleeman Pentaphonic
instruments.text: A five-voice synthesiser with 15 VCOs, a 37-note keyboard, a 600-note sequencer and built-in chorus, also sold in a transparent case as the Pentaphonic Clear.

instruments.name: Godwin String Concert 749
instruments.text: A 49-note string synthesiser with ten sliders for its string voices and effects.

instruments.name: Groove Electronics Stinger
instruments.text: A duophonic four-DCO MIDI rack module combining two EDP Wasp voices, with 46 knobs.

instruments.name: Groove Synthesis 3rd Wave
instruments.text: A 24-voice, four-part hybrid wavetable synth presented as a successor to the PPG Wave, with three wavetable or virtual-analogue oscillators and an analogue low-pass plus a digital filter per voice, later also in a desktop version.

instruments.name: Groove Synthesis 3rd Wave 8M
instruments.text: An eight-voice, bi-timbral desktop version of the 3rd Wave with the same three-oscillator engine and analogue filters, patch-compatible with the 24-voice models.

instruments.name: Hammond Solovox
instruments.text: A monophonic attachment instrument for the piano, with a three-octave mini keyboard and a tone cabinet holding a vacuum-tube oscillator and octave-divider circuits, giving lead organ and orchestral voices.

instruments.name: Hammond SY100
instruments.text: A 44-note monophonic synthesiser with Hammond's Autopatch preset system and a seven-by-seven grid of knobs.

instruments.name: Hartmann Neuron
instruments.text: A 61-key synthesiser using neural-network resynthesis, with two 'Resynator' oscillators per voice and a hard disk, designed by Axel Hartmann.

instruments.name: Hillwood Blue Comet 73
instruments.text: A Japanese 37-note monophonic synthesiser with ten sliders, over 20 rocker switches and pitch bend.

instruments.name: Hohner Hi-String
instruments.text: A string synthesiser with cello and string sounds, volume and decay sliders and a swell pedal.

instruments.name: Hohner K4 String Thing
instruments.text: A 49-note string synthesiser with four faders for the volume and decay of its cello and string sounds, and an ensemble effect.

instruments.name: Hohner Orchestral String Performer
instruments.text: A 60-note split multi-instrument keyboard with polyphonic clavichord, piano, cello, violin and viola sounds and a monophonic brass section.

instruments.name: IK Multimedia UNO Synth
instruments.text: A battery-powered analogue monosynth made with Soundmachines, with two VCOs, a two-pole OTA multimode filter, a 16-step sequencer and a 27-note touch keyboard.

instruments.name: IK Multimedia UNO Synth Pro
instruments.text: A three-oscillator paraphonic analogue synth with the UNO's OTA filter plus an SSI 2/4-pole low-pass filter, a 64-step sequencer and a 37-key Fatar keyboard, also sold as a desktop version.

instruments.name: IK Multimedia UNO Synth Pro X
instruments.text: A compact three-oscillator paraphonic analogue synth with OTA and SSI filters, analogue overdrive, ten digital effects and a 64-step sequencer.

instruments.name: Intellijel Cascadia
instruments.text: A desktop analogue semi-modular monosynth mixing East and West Coast synthesis, with two VCOs, a multimode filter, a wavefolder, utility sections and 101 patch points.

instruments.name: Ionic Performer
instruments.text: An American three-VCO monophonic synthesiser with a 49-note keyboard, pushbutton matrix patching and quadraphonic output.

instruments.name: Jen SX-1000
instruments.text: An Italian monophonic synthesiser with one DCO and a 37-note keyboard.

instruments.name: Jen SX-2000
instruments.text: A monophonic preset synthesiser with seven presets and a 44-note keyboard.

instruments.name: Kawai SX-210
instruments.text: An eight-voice programmable analogue polysynth with eight DCOs, eight 24dB/octave low-pass VCFs and a static high-pass filter, an ensemble circuit, a five-octave keyboard without velocity and 32 memories.

instruments.name: Kawai SX-240
instruments.text: An eight-voice analogue polysynth with 16 DCOs (two per voice, or four per voice in four-voice mode), a split at middle C, 48 memories and a 1,500-note real-time sequencer.

instruments.name: Kawai K3
instruments.text: A six-voice hybrid synth with two digital-waveform oscillators per voice, 31 factory waveforms and a user waveform built from the levels of 32 harmonics, an analogue resonant filter and a velocity- and pressure-sensitive five-octave keyboard; the rack K3m shares its engine.

instruments.name: Kawai K5
instruments.text: A 16-voice digital additive synth with up to 126 harmonics per sound, a digital dynamic filter and an 11-band formant filter, 15-part multitimbral operation and a velocity-sensitive keyboard; the K5m is its expander version.

instruments.name: Kawai K1
instruments.text: A 16-voice digital synth playing back 256 8-bit PCM waveforms (204 additive and 52 sampled), without filters, with a 61-key keyboard with velocity and aftertouch; also sold as the K1m and K1r modules and revised as the K1II with drum sounds.

instruments.name: Kawai K4
instruments.text: A 16-voice digital synth with four sources per patch drawn from 96 harmonic-based waveforms and 160 PCM waveforms, a digital resonant filter, built-in effects and a velocity- and pressure-sensitive five-octave keyboard; the K4r is its rack version.

instruments.name: Kawai Spectra
instruments.text: A budget 10-voice digital synth (KC10) using 16-bit PCM and harmonic-based waveforms, with 64 preset and 32 user sounds, preset rhythm patterns and no filters or aftertouch.

instruments.name: Kawai K11
instruments.text: A 32-voice, 32-part multitimbral digital synth playing 6MB of 16-bit samples through a resonant digital filter, with seven drum kits, reverb and a 61-key velocity- and pressure-sensitive keyboard.

instruments.name: Kawai K5000
instruments.text: A 32-voice additive synth with up to six sources per sound, each of up to 64 harmonics or a PCM sample with its own formant filter, sold as the K5000W workstation with sequencer, the K5000S with knobs and arpeggiator, and the K5000R rack.

instruments.name: Keynote Scorpion
instruments.text: A two-VCO monophonic synthesiser with a 44-note keyboard and aftertouch.

instruments.name: Korg Maxi-Korg 800DV
instruments.text: A dual-voice analogue synthesiser built as a version of the miniKORG 700 able to sound two voices at once.

instruments.name: Korg 900PS
instruments.text: A preset analogue synthesiser from Korg's mid-1970s range, offering a fixed selection of factory sounds.

instruments.name: Korg SB-100 Synthe Bass
instruments.text: A bass keyboard synthesiser from Korg's mid-1970s range.

instruments.name: Korg 770
instruments.text: The successor to the miniKORG 700S, an analogue monosynth with two VCOs and a ring modulator.

instruments.name: Korg PE-1000 Polyphonic Ensemble
instruments.text: Korg's first polyphonic synthesiser, a preset analogue keyboard with one VCO per note sharing a single filter and envelope, seven electric-piano presets and 61 keys, sold in the US as the Univox K4.

instruments.name: Korg PE-2000 Polyphonic Ensemble S
instruments.text: A preset string synthesiser with three detunable divide-down generators, each with its own modulation oscillator, a built-in phaser and eight presets including organ, brass, chorus and strings.

instruments.name: Korg PS-3100
instruments.text: A fully polyphonic patchable analogue synthesiser with a complete synthesiser voice board for each of its 48 keys.

instruments.name: Korg PS-3300
instruments.text: A patchable polyphonic analogue synthesiser that combines three PS-3100 units for 144 voices across 48 notes, played from the detachable PS-3010 keyboard with its X-Y Manipulator joystick, of which only around 30 to 50 were made.

instruments.name: Korg MS-10
instruments.text: The single-VCO member of Korg's semi-modular MS series, an analogue monosynth with one VCF, one envelope generator and a 32-key keyboard, known for its electro bass sounds.

instruments.name: Korg MS-50
instruments.text: The keyboardless module of Korg's semi-modular MS series, a patchable analogue synthesiser made to work alongside the MS-10, MS-20 and SQ-10 sequencer.

instruments.name: Korg PS-3200
instruments.text: A patchable polyphonic analogue synthesiser in the PS series with two voices per key, a 7-band equaliser in place of resonators and memory to save and recall 16 presets.

instruments.name: Korg Delta
instruments.text: A hybrid string machine and polysynth released alongside the Sigma and Lambda.

instruments.name: Korg Lambda
instruments.text: A preset polyphonic keyboard, the Lambda ES50, that combined string and piano voices, released alongside the Sigma and Delta.

instruments.name: Korg Sigma
instruments.text: A monophonic analogue synthesiser for organ players and live use, with two separately mixable engines called Synthe and Instrument, two modulation joysticks and an aftertouch-sensitive 37-key keyboard.

instruments.name: Korg Trident
instruments.text: A multi-section analogue synthesiser combining an eight-voice, two-VCO polysynth with separate string and brass sections that can be assigned to two regions of its 61-key keyboard, plus a flanger, followed by a MkII in 1982.

instruments.name: Korg Poly-61
instruments.text: A six-voice analogue polysynth with two digitally controlled oscillators per voice, 64 patch memories and a parameter-select interface in place of dedicated knobs, followed by the MIDI-equipped Poly-61M in 1984.

instruments.name: Korg Poly-800
instruments.text: An eight-voice synthesiser with digitally controlled oscillators sharing a single filter, battery power and a light body that could be strapped on, the first fully programmable polyphonic synthesiser sold for under $1,000, updated as the Poly-800 II in 1986.

instruments.name: Korg DW-6000
instruments.text: A six-voice hybrid synthesiser pairing two digital waveforms per voice, chosen from eight, with analogue filters and amplifiers, a chorus effect, 64 memories, a joystick and MIDI.

instruments.name: Korg EX-800
instruments.text: A keyboardless, rack-mountable version of the Poly-800 that could be paired with a Poly-800 over MIDI to increase polyphony.

instruments.name: Korg DW-8000
instruments.text: An eight-voice hybrid synthesiser with two digital waveforms per voice chosen from 16, a resonant analogue low-pass filter, a digital delay, an arpeggiator and a velocity- and aftertouch-sensitive 61-key keyboard.

instruments.name: Korg EX-8000
instruments.text: The rack-mounted counterpart of the DW-8000, with the same features except the arpeggiator.

instruments.name: Korg DSS-1
instruments.text: Korg's first sampling keyboard, an eight-voice instrument combining 12-bit sampling, additive synthesis and waveform drawing with an analogue filter path and a 61-key keyboard.

instruments.name: Korg 707
instruments.text: A more portable version of the DS-8 FM synthesiser, without its digital effects but with strap pegs for playing it as a keytar.

instruments.name: Korg DS-8
instruments.text: An eight-voice, four-operator FM synthesiser built with Yamaha components under licence, with an analogue-style interface for FM editing, and Korg's first multitimbral MIDI synthesiser.

instruments.name: Korg DSM-1
instruments.text: The rack-mounted version of the DSS-1 sampler, with 16-note polyphony, four times the memory, a high-density disk drive, individual outputs and a multitimbral mode.

instruments.name: Korg M1
instruments.text: A 16-voice, eight-part sample-based workstation with 4 MB of PCM waveforms, effects, a sequencer and a 61-key keyboard, with an estimated 250,000 units sold.

instruments.name: Korg M3R
instruments.text: A cost-reduced rack-mount sound module derived from the M1R.

instruments.name: Korg T1/T2/T3
instruments.text: A series of workstations that improved on the M1, with 190 multisounds and 85 drum samples in 8 MB of PCM.

instruments.name: Korg Wavestation
instruments.text: A 32-voice vector synthesiser with four digital oscillators, wave sequencing of PCM waveforms, a vector joystick and a 61-key keyboard, co-designed with Dave Smith, whose 1991 EX version doubled the sample ROM.

instruments.name: Korg 01/W
instruments.text: A workstation series using Korg's AI² synthesis, with 255 multisounds in 6 MB of PCM, waveshaping, effects and a sequencer, sold as the 61-key 01/W and 01/Wfd, the 76-key 01/Wpro and the 88-key 01/WproX.

instruments.name: Korg Wavestation A/D
instruments.text: The first rack-mount Wavestation, adding an extra RAM bank and analogue inputs that could be processed by its effects or fed into wave sequences.

instruments.name: Korg Wavestation SR
instruments.text: A 1U rack-mount Wavestation with a 16-by-2 character display and no joystick, marketed as a preset module with eight ROM banks.

instruments.name: Korg X3
instruments.text: A General MIDI workstation using an enhanced AI² engine with 340 multisamples, a sequencer and a Fatar keyboard, joined in 1994 by the 76-key X2.

instruments.name: Korg X3R
instruments.text: The rack-mounted counterpart of the X3 workstation, with all of its features in a 19-inch rack format.

instruments.name: Korg 05R/W
instruments.text: A 32-voice AI² half-rack synthesiser module with General MIDI, the rack version of the X5, with a serial connection for a Mac or PC.

instruments.name: Korg X5
instruments.text: A 61-key, 32-voice, 16-part multitimbral AI² synthesiser with General MIDI, using the X3's engine without its floppy drive or sequencer.

instruments.name: Korg Prophecy
instruments.text: A monophonic DSP synthesiser using Korg's MOSS engine for analogue modelling, FM and physical modelling, with two oscillators, two multimode filters, a 37-key keyboard and a log-shaped controller wheel with a ribbon.

instruments.name: Korg Trinity
instruments.text: A 32-voice PCM workstation, the first instrument with a large touchscreen, with expansion options for sampling, hard-disk recording and Prophecy or MOSS synth boards, in 61-, 76- and 88-key models.

instruments.name: Korg X5D
instruments.text: An AI² synthesiser keyboard with 64-note polyphony and an additional set of patches over the X5, the keyboard counterpart of the X5DR.

instruments.name: Korg X5DR
instruments.text: A half-rack AI² module similar to the 05R/W but with 64-note polyphony and an additional set of patches.

instruments.name: Korg N364/N264
instruments.text: A 64-voice AI² workstation with 8 MB of sample ROM, the first Korg keyboard with Realtime Pattern Play and Record (RPPR), in 61-key (N364) and 76-key (N264) versions.

instruments.name: Korg NS5R
instruments.text: A half-rack AI² module with 64-note polyphony and a large LCD.

instruments.name: Korg Z1
instruments.text: A 12-voice, six-part MOSS synthesiser for physical and analogue modelling, with two modelling oscillators per voice, a polyphonic arpeggiator, an XY touchpad and a 61-key keyboard.

instruments.name: Korg N1
instruments.text: An 88-key piano-action AI² synthesiser, an expanded N5 with a larger sample ROM and support for GM, GS and XG.

instruments.name: Korg N1R
instruments.text: The rack-mount version of the N1 AI² synthesiser.

instruments.name: Korg N5
instruments.text: A keyboard version of the NS5R AI² sound module, without its expansion slot.

instruments.name: Korg TR-Rack
instruments.text: A 1U rack-module version of the Trinity, without expansion slots but with a larger internal sample ROM.

instruments.name: Korg NX5R
instruments.text: The successor to the NS5R half-rack module, adding a set of XG-compatible sounds on a daughterboard.

instruments.name: Korg Triton
instruments.text: A sampling and sequencing workstation using Korg's HI synthesis with a touchscreen, the successor to the Trinity and Korg's first keyboard with sampling since the DSS-1.

instruments.name: Korg MS2000
instruments.text: A four-voice virtual analogue synthesiser with two oscillators per voice, a resonant multimode filter, a vocoder and a 44-key keyboard, meant to bring the MS-10 and MS-20's sound back through modelling, updated as the MS2000B in 2003.

instruments.name: Korg MS2000R
instruments.text: The rack-mount version of the MS2000 virtual analogue synthesiser, updated as the MS2000BR in 2003.

instruments.name: Korg Triton-Rack
instruments.text: A 2U rack-mount version of the Triton with a smaller LCD in place of the touchscreen, sampling, and room for eight PCM expansion boards.

instruments.name: Korg KARMA
instruments.text: A 62-voice, 16-part workstation in the Triton family with Kay's Algorithmic Real-time Music Architecture for generating phrases, and a 61-key keyboard.

instruments.name: Korg microKORG
instruments.text: A compact virtual analogue synthesiser and vocoder built around the MS2000's DSP engine, with a programmable step arpeggiator and an eight-band vocoder.

instruments.name: Korg Triton Le
instruments.text: A cost-reduced Triton without the touchscreen, ribbon or floppy drive, with a SmartMedia slot and one insert effect, in 61-, 76- and 88-key versions.

instruments.name: Korg Triton Studio
instruments.text: A Triton workstation with about double the polyphony, S/PDIF input and output, a piano expansion board and an onboard CD-R drive.

instruments.name: Korg Triton Extreme
instruments.text: A Triton workstation with the Studio's sample ROM plus several expansion libraries, a touchscreen, USB and Valve Force circuitry using a vacuum tube.

instruments.name: Korg OASYS
instruments.text: A workstation running a custom Linux operating system on PC-like hardware, with several synthesis engines including sample playback, wave sequencing and physical modelling, in 76- and 88-key versions, of which just over 3,000 were sold.

instruments.name: Korg RADIAS
instruments.text: A 24-voice virtual analogue synthesiser and vocoder using Korg's MMT engine, with two oscillators, two filters and a wave shaper per voice, sold with a keyboard or as a module.

instruments.name: Korg TR
instruments.text: A Triton Le-type workstation with expanded ROM, additional programs and combinations, USB and an SD card slot.

instruments.name: Korg M3
instruments.text: A 120-voice PCM workstation and sampler with Enhanced Definition Synthesis based on the OASYS's HD-1 engine, the successor to the Triton, in 61-, 73- and 88-key and module versions.

instruments.name: Korg microX
instruments.text: A compact synthesiser with the X50's HI synthesis engine and an extended ROM focused on drum and percussion samples.

instruments.name: Korg R3
instruments.text: A portable version of the RADIAS virtual analogue synthesiser.

instruments.name: Korg X50
instruments.text: A low-cost synthesiser with the TR's HI synthesis engine and extended ROM, without a sequencer or expansion.

instruments.name: Korg M50
instruments.text: A stripped-down version of the M3 workstation with the same EDS sound system but less polyphony and no expansion or sampling.

instruments.name: Korg microKORG XL
instruments.text: The successor to the microKORG, using the MMT engine from the RADIAS and R3 and adding keyboard staples such as electric piano and CX-3 organ, updated with new sounds as the microKORG XL+ in 2012.

instruments.name: Korg microSTATION
instruments.text: A workstation with mini keys, part of Korg's micro series.

instruments.name: Korg Monotron
instruments.text: A miniature analogue monosynth with a sawtooth VCO, a VCF based on the MS-20's and a ribbon controller marked with 18 keys.

instruments.name: Korg PS60
instruments.text: A performance synthesiser designed for the gigging musician.

instruments.name: Korg Kronos
instruments.text: The successor to the OASYS, a workstation combining nine synthesiser engines with a sequencer, digital recorder, effects and a colour touchscreen in 61-, 73- and 88-key versions, later updated as the Kronos X, Kronos 2 and a 2025 Kronos.

instruments.name: Korg Monotron Delay
instruments.text: A development of the Monotron with one sawtooth VCO, an LFO with two wave shapes, a VCF and a delay, played from a ribbon controller.

instruments.name: Korg Monotron Duo
instruments.text: A development of the Monotron with two square-wave VCOs, cross-modulation and a VCF, played from a ribbon controller.

instruments.name: Korg Krome
instruments.text: A mid-price workstation with sounds derived from the Kronos.

instruments.name: Korg KingKORG
instruments.text: A 61-key virtual analogue synthesiser designed for live performance, with modelling filters that reproduce the sound of earlier instruments.

instruments.name: Korg Kross
instruments.text: A mobile synthesiser workstation keyboard.

instruments.name: Korg MS-20 mini
instruments.text: A reissue of the MS-20 at 86% of the original's size, developed by the original's engineers to replicate its circuits, adding a MIDI input and USB MIDI.

instruments.name: Korg Volca Bass
instruments.text: An analogue bass synthesiser with three VCOs, a VCF, a one-octave touch-plate keyboard and a step sequencer, released alongside the Volca Keys and Volca Beats.

instruments.name: Korg Volca Keys
instruments.text: A three-voice paraphonic analogue synthesiser with one VCO per voice, a shared VCF, a touch-plate keyboard, a 16-step sequencer and battery power.

instruments.name: Korg MS-20 Kit
instruments.text: A full-size, unassembled MS-20 made in very small numbers, adding MIDI and USB and a choice between the filters of the earlier and later original MS-20s.

instruments.name: Korg RK-100S
instruments.text: A 37-key keytar synthesiser that is essentially a keytar version of the microKORG XL+.

instruments.name: Korg ARP Odyssey
instruments.text: Korg's revival of the ARP Odyssey duophonic analogue synthesiser at 86% of the original's size, developed with advice from ARP co-founder David Friend.

instruments.name: Korg MS-20M Kit
instruments.text: An unassembled desktop module version of the MS-20 sold with the SQ-1 step sequencer, adding oscillator sync, FM, a pulse-width modulation input and a choice of the original filter designs.

instruments.name: Korg ARP Odyssey Module
instruments.text: A desktop module version of Korg's ARP Odyssey reissue with two VCOs, duophonic playing, three selectable filter types, CV, gate and trigger jacks and USB MIDI, in Rev1 and Rev3 styles.

instruments.name: Korg microKORG S
instruments.text: A slightly updated microKORG virtual analogue synthesiser and vocoder with a built-in 2+1 speaker system and a white body.

instruments.name: Korg Minilogue
instruments.text: A four-voice analogue polysynth with two VCOs per voice, two- and four-pole resonant low-pass filters, 200 presets, a polyphonic step sequencer and 37 slim keys, designed by Tatsuya Takahashi.

instruments.name: Korg Volca FM
instruments.text: A three-voice digital FM synthesiser in the compact, battery-powered volca format with a built-in step sequencer.

instruments.name: Korg ARP Odyssey FS
instruments.text: A full-size, limited-edition ARP Odyssey reissue with a standard keyboard, assembled in New York, in designs reproducing the Rev1, Rev2 and Rev3 originals.

instruments.name: Korg Kross 2
instruments.text: The successor to the Kross, a lightweight, battery-powered workstation with more than a thousand preset sounds and added expansion PCM memory.

instruments.name: Korg Monologue
instruments.text: A monophonic analogue synthesiser with two VCOs, an MS-20-style filter chip, a drive control, microtuning, a step sequencer and 25 slim keys, developed with Richard D. James.

instruments.name: Korg Prologue
instruments.text: An analogue polysynth with a digital multi-engine and DSP effects, the flagship of the minilogue and monologue series, sold as the 16-voice, 61-key prologue-16 and the eight-voice, 49-key prologue-8.

instruments.name: Korg Minilogue XD
instruments.text: A four-voice analogue polysynth with two VCOs per voice plus a digital multi-engine, digital effects, an expanded sequencer and microtuning.

instruments.name: Korg Minilogue XD Module
instruments.text: The desktop version of the minilogue xd four-voice analogue synthesiser, with the keyboard version's controls and a poly-chain function linking two units for up to eight voices.

instruments.name: Korg Nu:Tekt NTS-1
instruments.text: A solder-free DIY digital monosynth kit with one digital oscillator, a multimode filter, three LFOs, three effects, an arpeggiator, a ribbon controller and support for custom oscillators and effects through the logue SDK.

instruments.name: Korg Volca Modular
instruments.text: A battery-powered West-coast-style semi-modular analogue synthesiser with a complex oscillator, low-pass gates, function generators, patch cables and a 16-step sequencer.

instruments.name: Korg Volca Nubass
instruments.text: A vacuum-tube-based analogue synthesiser in the volca format designed for acid-style bass sounds.

instruments.name: Korg ARP 2600 FS
instruments.text: A limited-edition reproduction of the ARP 2600 semi-modular synthesiser, handcrafted in Japan, adding USB and MIDI and XLR outputs, with a duophonic 49-key 3620 keyboard with an arpeggiator and sequencer.

instruments.name: Korg Opsix
instruments.text: An altered-FM synthesiser with a three-octave keyboard and an operator mixer, whose operators can perform FM, ring modulation and filter FM or act as filters or wavefolders.

instruments.name: Korg Wavestate
instruments.text: A wave-sequencing synthesiser with 37 keys, a tribute to the Wavestation, later offered as the 96-voice wavestate mkII and the 61-key wavestate SE in 2023.

instruments.name: Korg ARP 2600 M
instruments.text: A smaller, keyless version of Korg's ARP 2600 FS semi-modular synthesiser in a more compact and portable format.

instruments.name: Korg miniKORG 700FS
instruments.text: A limited-edition revival of the two-oscillator miniKORG 700S analogue monosynth, adding an arpeggiator, spring reverb and aftertouch.

instruments.name: Korg Modwave
instruments.text: A wavetable synthesiser with Kaoss Physics and Motion Sequencing that builds on the DW-8000's combination of digital wavetables and filters, later updated as the 60-voice modwave mkII.

instruments.name: Korg MS-20 FS
instruments.text: A full-size, factory-assembled MS-20 reissue with 37 keys, a patch panel, MIDI and USB, made in four limited-edition colours.

instruments.name: Korg Nautilus
instruments.text: The successor to the Kronos 2, a workstation running the Kronos's nine sound engines on an x86 processor and Linux, in 61-, 73- and 88-key versions, followed by the aftertouch Nautilus AT in 2023.

instruments.name: Korg Volca FM2
instruments.text: The second-generation volca fm, a six-voice FM synthesiser with six operators and 32 algorithms that is compatible with Yamaha DX7 SysEx patches.

instruments.name: Korg KingKORG NEO
instruments.text: A compact 37-key virtual analogue synthesiser using Korg's XMT engine, with filters modelled on five earlier synthesisers and a vocoder.

instruments.name: Korg microKORG 2
instruments.text: A successor to the microKORG with a new sound engine, a vocoder with a dedicated microphone, a loop recorder, an arpeggiator and a mini keyboard.

instruments.name: Korg Modwave Module
instruments.text: A desktop and rack-mount version of the modwave mkII wavetable synthesiser with 60 stereo voices.

instruments.name: Korg Multi/Poly
