instruments.text: A 60-voice analogue-modelling synthesiser in the opsix and wavestate format with three oscillator types, Kaoss Physics, Motion Sequencing 2.0 and virtual voice cards that model analogue component variation.

instruments.name: Korg Opsix Module
instruments.text: A desktop and rack-mount version of the opsix altered-FM synthesiser with 64 voices instead of the original's 32.

instruments.name: Korg Wavestate Module
instruments.text: A desktop and rack-mount version of the wavestate mkII wave-sequencing synthesiser with 120 voices and MIDI 2.0 Property Exchange support.

instruments.name: Korg miniKORG 700Sm
instruments.text: A revival of the two-oscillator miniKORG 700S that keeps the features of the miniKORG 700FS with a slimmer keyboard and a recreation of the Traveler filter controller.

instruments.name: Korg Multi/Poly Module
instruments.text: A 19-inch desktop and rack-mount version of the multi/poly analogue-modelling synthesiser with MIDI 2.0 Property Exchange and poly aftertouch support.

instruments.name: Korg PS-3300 FS
instruments.text: A full-scale reissue of the PS-3300 developed with its original designer Fumio Mieda, with three patchable synth layers across 49 keys and voices, 256 memory slots, USB and MIDI.

instruments.name: Kurzweil 150
instruments.text: A rack-mount instrument using Fourier additive synthesis for acoustic emulation and sound modelling.

instruments.name: Kurzweil RMX
instruments.text: An eight-space rack-module version of the K250.

instruments.name: Kurzweil 1000 GX
instruments.text: A guitar expander module in the K1000 family, with optional soundblocks.

instruments.name: Kurzweil 1000 HX
instruments.text: A horn expander module in the K1000 family, with optional soundblocks.

instruments.name: Kurzweil 1000 PX
instruments.text: A professional expander module identical in sound to the K1000.

instruments.name: Kurzweil 1000 SX
instruments.text: A string expander module in the K1000 family, with optional soundblocks.

instruments.name: Kurzweil K1000
instruments.text: A 76-note sample-playback keyboard bringing the K250's sample libraries to a cheaper instrument, expandable with ROM soundblocks, with an 88-note version sold as the K1200.

instruments.name: Kurzweil K2000
instruments.text: A 61-note keyboard, also sold as a three-space rack, introducing Variable Architecture Synthesis Technology (V.A.S.T.), with an optional sampling version.

instruments.name: Kurzweil K2500
instruments.text: The successor to the K2000, sold first as a three-space rack and then as 76-note and 88-note keyboards, with optional sampling.

instruments.name: Kurzweil K2600
instruments.text: The K2500's replacement, with a stereo piano ROM block, the KDFX effects engine as standard and Triple Modular Processing, sold in keyboard and rack versions and later as the 61-key K2661.

instruments.name: Kurzweil PC2
instruments.text: A 76-note or 88-note performance controller with a 64-voice V.A.S.T.-based sound engine, expandable to 128 voices, and KDFX-based effects.

instruments.name: Kurzweil PC3
instruments.text: A performance controller with a next-generation V.A.S.T. synthesis engine derived from the K2000 series.

instruments.name: Kurzweil PC4
instruments.text: An 88-note weighted performance controller with 256 voices, 2 GB of factory samples, a six-operator FM synthesizer, the VA-1 virtual analogue engine and tonewheel organ modelling.

instruments.name: Kurzweil K2700
instruments.text: A flagship workstation released with an 88-key graded-hammer weighted keyboard.

instruments.name: Logan String Melody
instruments.text: A 49-note string synthesiser with a splittable keyboard, followed by the functionally identical String Melody II.

instruments.name: Logan String Orchestra
instruments.text: A 49-note string synthesiser with portamento.

instruments.name: Logan Vocal Synth
instruments.text: A 60-note multi-instrument keyboard with string, vocal and monosynth sections.

instruments.name: Lord Skywave
instruments.text: A British two-VCO monophonic synthesiser with a 49-note keyboard and joystick modulation.

instruments.name: Make Noise 0-Coast
instruments.text: A single-voice patchable analogue synthesizer mixing Moog and Buchla approaches, with an oscillator, a Slope generator, a Contour envelope and MIDI, playable with or without patch cables.

instruments.name: Make Noise Strega
instruments.text: A patchable analogue instrument made with Alessandro Cortini, with an oscillator, a degrading delay, a filter, a function generator and touch plates, built for textures and imperfect sounds.

instruments.name: MFB Kraftzwerg
instruments.text: A semi-modular analogue monosynth based on MFB's Synth II, with three VCOs, a resonant 24dB low-pass filter, ring modulator, two envelopes, two LFOs and 37 patch points over pre-wired routing.

instruments.name: MFB Dominion X
instruments.text: A programmable analogue desktop monosynth with three VCOs, ring modulation, a six-mode multimode filter, three LFOs, 128 patches and CV inputs for modular use.

instruments.name: MFB Dominion 1
instruments.text: A programmable analogue mono and paraphonic synth with three VCOs, a multimode filter, a 26-point patch panel, sequencer and a three-octave Fatar keyboard.

instruments.name: MFB Dominion Club
instruments.text: A compact desktop monosynth based on the Dominion 1, with two analogue and one digital oscillator, two sub-oscillators, a 24dB multimode filter, a sequencer and 100 memories.

instruments.name: Modal Electronics 008
instruments.text: An eight-voice analogue polysynth with two VCOs and two sub-oscillators per voice, multi-mode filters, a 32-step sequencer, a touchscreen and a five-octave Fatar keyboard with aftertouch.

instruments.name: Modal Electronics CRAFTsynth
instruments.text: A small self-assembly digital monophonic synth kit with two oscillators, up to eight detunable sub-oscillators in unison mode, a resonant low-pass filter and a five-note touch panel, later followed by the wavetable CRAFTsynth 2.0.

instruments.name: Modal Electronics Skulpt
instruments.text: A portable four-voice digital virtual-analogue synth with eight oscillators per voice, a 16-key touch keyboard, a sequencer and battery power.

instruments.name: Modal Electronics Argon8
instruments.text: An eight-voice digital wavetable synth with four oscillators per voice, effects, an arpeggiator and a sequencer, sold with 37 keys and later also as the 61-key Argon8X.

instruments.name: Modal Electronics Argon8M
instruments.text: A desktop and 3U rackmount version of the eight-voice Argon8 wavetable synth with 32 wavetable oscillators.

instruments.name: Modal Electronics Cobalt8
instruments.text: An eight-voice virtual-analogue synth with up to eight oscillators per voice, a four-pole resonant ladder-style filter, a joystick and 37 keys with aftertouch, later also sold as the 61-key Cobalt8X.

instruments.name: Modal Electronics Cobalt8M
instruments.text: A desktop and rack version of the Cobalt8 with the same eight-voice, 64-oscillator virtual-analogue engine, ladder filter and effects.

instruments.name: Modal Electronics Cobalt5S
instruments.text: A compact five-voice virtual-analogue synth on the Cobalt engine, with up to eight oscillators per voice, a morphable ladder filter, MPE support, an X/Y/Z touchpad and 37 compact keys.

instruments.name: Modal Electronics Carbon8
instruments.text: An eight-voice digital synthesizer with two oscillators per voice drawing on 56 core waveforms, 34 filter types and three effects slots, released after Modal's takeover by Alltronics.

instruments.name: Modal Electronics Carbon8M
instruments.text: A desktop and 3U rack version of the Carbon8 with the same digital engine and a joystick in place of the keys.

instruments.name: Modulus 002
instruments.text: A twelve-voice analogue/digital hybrid polysynth designed and built in the UK, launched by Modulus before the company was renamed Modal Electronics in 2015.

instruments.name: Moog Model 12
instruments.text: A compact modular system that followed the Model 10, with oscillators of greater pitch stability and a new keyboard design.

instruments.name: Moog Sonic Six
instruments.text: A duophonic two-oscillator synthesizer with a 49-key keyboard and a built-in speaker, in a briefcase whose control panel folds over the keys, developed from the muSonics Sonic V for education.

instruments.name: Moog Model 15
instruments.text: The smallest of Moog's 1970s modular systems, in a portable suitcase-style enclosure, with two oscillators, two VCAs and a lowpass filter.

instruments.name: Moog Satellite
instruments.text: A preset monophonic synthesizer for the home organ market with one oscillator, bandpass and lowpass filters and preset timbres such as Brass, Reeds, Strings, Bell and Lunar; Thomas Organ also built it as the Thomas 1055.

instruments.name: Moog System 35
instruments.text: A mid-sized Moog modular system in a wedge-shaped housing, aimed at studios and education.

instruments.name: Moog System 55
instruments.text: The largest of Moog's 1970s modular systems, with the biggest complement of modules the company offered.

instruments.name: Moog Micromoog
instruments.text: A low-cost monosynth with one oscillator plus a sub-octave, a 24 dB lowpass filter, two attack-release envelopes, a 32-note keyboard and a ribbon controller for pitch.

instruments.name: Moog Minitmoog
instruments.text: A two-oscillator preset monosynth with a 37-note keyboard, aftertouch, oscillator sync and presets such as Trumpet, Oboe, Clarinet and Violin; an upgraded Satellite, made only until 1976.

instruments.name: Moog Polymoog
instruments.text: A fully polyphonic hybrid synthesizer using divide-down oscillators, with a 71-note weighted, touch-sensitive keyboard split into three sections; also known for limited programmability and reliability problems.

instruments.name: Moog Taurus I
instruments.text: A bass synthesizer played from 13 organ-style foot pedals, with two oscillators and a 24 dB resonant lowpass filter, meant to be played by foot while the hands played keyboards, and taken up by guitarists too.

instruments.name: Moog Multimoog
instruments.text: A two-oscillator monosynth developed from the Micromoog, with a 24 dB lowpass filter, sample-and-hold and a 44-note keyboard with aftertouch, one of the first synthesizers to offer it.

instruments.name: Moog Polymoog Keyboard
instruments.text: A stripped-down, cheaper version of the Polymoog whose Vox Humana preset gave Gary Numan his string sound.

instruments.name: Moog Prodigy
instruments.text: A two-oscillator monosynth with a 4-pole ladder lowpass filter and a 32-key keyboard, which gave the band The Prodigy its name.

instruments.name: Moog Liberation
instruments.text: One of the first keytars, with two monophonic oscillators, a paraphonic organ section, an aftertouch keyboard and a ribbon for pitch bend on the neck, cabled to a rack unit.

instruments.name: Moog Opus 3
instruments.text: A divide-down ensemble keyboard with string, brass and organ sections, a 4-pole multimode filter and a 49-key keyboard, designed by Herbert Deutsch and known mainly for its organ sounds.

instruments.name: Moog Rogue
instruments.text: A low-cost two-oscillator monosynth with a voltage-controlled lowpass filter and a 32-key keyboard.

instruments.name: Moog Taurus II
instruments.text: A cheaper successor to the Taurus I with 18 foot pedals, two oscillators with an added pulse wave, no patch memory and a raised control panel.

instruments.name: Moog Little Phatty
instruments.text: A two-oscillator analogue monosynth with 37 keys and 100 patch memories, the last instrument Robert Moog helped design and the first Moog released after his death.

instruments.name: Minimoog Voyager Old School
instruments.text: A Minimoog Voyager without the touch pad or MIDI, with keyboard pitch and gate CV outputs instead.

instruments.name: Minimoog Voyager XL
instruments.text: A Minimoog Voyager with a 61-note keyboard, a ribbon controller and a patch bay on the left, released for the Minimoog's 40th anniversary.

instruments.name: Moog Slim Phatty
instruments.text: The Little Phatty's analogue engine with no keyboard, for desktop or rack: two oscillators, a 24 dB ladder filter, an arpeggiator and MIDI, USB and CV control.

instruments.name: Moog Taurus 3
instruments.text: A limited run of 1,000 bass pedal synthesizers rebuilt on the Taurus I circuits, with 13 pedals and two oscillators, adding an LFO, patch memory, MIDI and USB.

instruments.name: Moog Minitaur
instruments.text: A compact analogue bass synthesizer with two oscillators, a ladder filter and two ADSR envelopes, the first of Moog's Taurus family without foot pedals.

instruments.name: Moog Sub Phatty
instruments.text: A 25-key analogue monosynth with two variable-waveshape oscillators, a square-wave sub oscillator, noise, a ladder filter with Multidrive and 16 presets.

instruments.name: Moog Emerson Modular System
instruments.text: A recreation of Keith Emerson's Moog modular, hand-built in a handful of units from the original documentation, circuit boards and panel artwork.

instruments.name: Moog Sub 37
instruments.text: A 37-key analogue synthesizer on the Sub Phatty engine, with two oscillators plus a sub oscillator, a Duo mode for two notes, an arpeggiator and step sequencer, aftertouch and 256 presets.

instruments.name: Moog Werkstatt-01
instruments.text: A no-solder kit synthesizer with one Moog oscillator, a 4-pole ladder filter, an LFO with audio-rate modulation, an ADS envelope and a patchable header, first built at Moogfest 2014.

instruments.name: Moog Model 15 (2015)
instruments.text: A hand-built recreation of the 1973 Model 15 in a run of 150, made from the original circuit board films with photo-etched aluminium panels.

instruments.name: Moog Mother-32
instruments.text: A tabletop semi-modular with one oscillator, a ladder filter switchable between lowpass and highpass, a 32-step sequencer, a 13-note keypad and a 32-point patch bay, removable as a Eurorack module.

instruments.name: Moog System 35 (2015)
instruments.text: A hand-built recreation of the 1973 System 35 in a run of 35, made from the original circuit board films with photo-etched aluminium panels.

instruments.name: Moog System 55 (2015)
instruments.text: A hand-built recreation of the 1973 System 55 in a run of 55, made from the original circuit board films with photo-etched aluminium panels.

instruments.name: Minimoog Model D (2016)
instruments.text: The Model D rebuilt on its original sound engine after some 30 years, adding a velocity-sensitive keyboard, MIDI, CV outputs, an analogue LFO and the mixer overload modification.

instruments.name: Moog Subsequent 37
instruments.text: The successor to the Sub 37, with a new keybed, doubled mixer headroom, a reworked ladder filter and retuned Multidrive.

instruments.name: Moog One
instruments.text: A tri-timbral analogue polysynth in 8- and 16-voice versions, with three VCOs and two independent filters per voice and a sequencer, arpeggiator and effects for each timbre; Moog's first analogue polysynth in over 35 years.

instruments.name: Moog Matriarch
instruments.text: A semi-modular with a 49-key keyboard, four oscillators playable as four-note paraphonic and 90 patch points, working with no cables.

instruments.name: Moog Model 10 (2019)
instruments.text: A limited, hand-built reissue of the 1971 Model 10 to the original specification, with eleven modules including three 900-series oscillators, a lowpass filter and the 907 fixed filter bank.

instruments.name: Moog Sirin
instruments.text: A limited desktop synthesizer of 2,500 units built on the Taurus sound engine, with two oscillators able to reach far above middle C, a 4-pole ladder filter, two ADSR envelopes and an LFO.

instruments.name: Moog Subharmonicon
instruments.text: A semi-modular polyrhythmic synthesizer with two VCOs, four subharmonic oscillators, two four-step sequencers and four rhythm generators, playing six-tone subharmonic chords.

instruments.name: Moog Subsequent 25
instruments.text: A 25-key analogue synthesizer replacing the Sub Phatty, with a two-note paraphonic Duo mode and a ladder filter with reworked gain staging.

instruments.name: Moog Mavis
instruments.text: A no-solder kit semi-modular with Moog oscillator and filter circuits, the first analogue wavefolder on a Moog instrument, a one-octave keyboard and 24 patch points, usable as a 44HP Eurorack module.

instruments.name: Moog Labyrinth
instruments.text: A 60HP semi-modular with newly designed oscillators, a wavefolder, a state-variable filter, dual generative sequencers and 32 patch points.

instruments.name: Moog Muse
instruments.text: An eight-voice bi-timbral analogue polysynth with two VCOs and a modulation VCO per voice, dual ladder filters, a 61-key keyboard with aftertouch and a stereo Diffusion Delay.

instruments.name: Moog Spectravox
instruments.text: A semi-modular spectral processor with a 10-band analogue filter bank, one Moog oscillator and noise, playable as a synthesizer or an analogue vocoder, with a patch bay.

instruments.name: Moog Messenger
instruments.text: A 32-key analogue monosynth with two variable-shape oscillators with wavefolders, a sub oscillator, a pole-mixing ladder filter, a 64-step sequencer and 256 presets.

instruments.name: Aelita
instruments.text: A Soviet monophonic analogue synthesiser with three oscillators, a resonant low-pass filter, a 44-key keyboard and a hinged lid over its control panel.

instruments.name: Synclavier II
instruments.text: A digital synthesizer using additive and FM synthesis, with sampling, a 32-track memory recorder and the ORK keyboard.

instruments.name: Synclavier PSMT
instruments.text: A Synclavier system built on the faster ABLE Model C processor, with Multi-Channel-Distribution digitally controlled analogue signal routing.

instruments.name: Synclavier 3200
instruments.text: A successor to the Synclavier PSMT in the Macintosh-based Synclavier range.

instruments.name: Synclavier 9600
instruments.text: The largest model of the Macintosh-based Synclavier range, operated with a Macintosh II as its terminal.

instruments.name: Novation Bass Station
instruments.text: A monophonic synth with digitally controlled oscillators, joined in 1994 by the Bass Station Rack with dual ADSR envelopes, a 12/24dB filter and oscillator sync.

instruments.name: Novation Super Bass Station
instruments.text: A development of the Bass Station that added an arpeggiator, a noise source, a ring modulator, a second LFO and a sub-oscillator.

instruments.name: Novation Supernova
instruments.text: A 3U rack-mount virtual analogue polysynth with 16-note polyphony (expandable), eight audio outputs and 56 programmable effects across its eight parts.

instruments.name: Novation Nova
instruments.text: A desktop performance module with the Supernova's synth engine and a 40-band vocoder.

instruments.name: Novation Supernova II
instruments.text: A virtual analogue polysynth in 24-, 36- and 48-voice models, sold as a 3U rack and as a 61-note keyboard, adding FM synthesis, an eight-part arpeggiator and a vocoder.

instruments.name: Novation A-Station
instruments.text: A compact analogue-modelling synth module with eight-voice polyphony, FM synthesis and a 12-voice vocoder.

instruments.name: Novation K-Station
instruments.text: A two-octave keyboard version of the A-Station with eight-voice polyphony, three oscillators and FM synthesis.

instruments.name: Novation KS Series
instruments.text: Enhanced versions of the K-Station engine with four-part multitimbral operation, sold as the four-octave KS4, the five-octave KS5 and the KS Rack.

instruments.name: Novation X-Station
instruments.text: A keyboard synth with an eight-voice Supernova-class engine and a built-in audio interface, designed with a computer sequencer to make a complete music-making set-up.

instruments.name: Novation XioSynth
instruments.text: A keyboard synthesiser with a USB audio interface and template-based MIDI control, in 25- and 49-key versions.

instruments.name: Novation UltraNova
instruments.text: A USB bus-powered, single-part analogue-modelling synth in the Nova series with 18 voices and wavetable synthesis.

instruments.name: Novation MiniNova
instruments.text: A micro synth with a 37-note keyboard and up to 18 voices, built around the same synth engine as the UltraNova.

instruments.name: Novation Bass Station II
instruments.text: An analogue monosynth reworking the original Bass Station concept, with three oscillators and two filters.

instruments.name: Novation Circuit Mono Station
instruments.text: An analogue paraphonic synthesiser in the Circuit family, played from its own sequencer.

instruments.name: Novation Peak
instruments.text: An eight-voice digital/analogue hybrid polysynth with digital oscillators and analogue filters.

instruments.name: Novation Summit
instruments.text: A 16-voice polyphonic flagship synthesiser with a 61-key keyboard.

instruments.name: Oberheim OB-Mx
instruments.text: An analogue synthesiser produced under Gibson's ownership of the Oberheim name, in collaboration with D. N. 'Lynx' Crowe and Don Buchla.

instruments.name: Oberheim OB-12
instruments.text: An analogue-modelling synthesiser developed by Viscount and sold under the Oberheim name.

instruments.name: Oberheim OB-X8
instruments.text: An eight-voice analogue polysynth combining the voice architectures of the OB-X, OB-Xa and OB-8, including their original presets, built in collaboration with Sequential.

instruments.name: Oberheim TEO-5
instruments.text: A compact five-voice analogue polysynth with VCOs, an SEM-style filter morphing between low-pass, notch and high-pass with a band-pass mode, and a 64-step polyphonic sequencer.

instruments.name: Oberheim Eight Voice
instruments.text: A polyphonic synthesiser combining eight SEM modules with a digitally scanned keyboard developed by Dave Rossum.

instruments.name: Oberheim Four Voice
instruments.text: A polyphonic synthesiser combining four SEM modules with a digitally scanned keyboard developed by Dave Rossum.

instruments.name: Oberheim OB-1
instruments.text: A monophonic analogue synthesiser described as the first completely programmable synthesiser.

instruments.name: Oberheim OB-SX
instruments.text: A preset analogue polysynth with two, four or six voices of two VCOs each and a 48-key keyboard, designed as a smaller live-performance version of the OB-X.

instruments.name: Oberheim Xpander
instruments.text: A six-voice keyboardless analogue synthesiser with 12 VCOs and a multimode filter offering 15 variations.

instruments.name: Oberheim Matrix-12
instruments.text: A twelve-voice analogue polysynth with 24 VCOs, in effect two Xpanders with a 61-key velocity-sensitive keyboard.

instruments.name: Oberheim Matrix-6
instruments.text: A six-voice, two-part multitimbral analogue polysynth with 12 digitally controlled oscillators and a low-pass filter, followed in 1986 by the keyboardless Matrix-6R.

instruments.name: Oberheim Matrix-1000
instruments.text: A low-cost monotimbral rack version of the Matrix-6 engine with 1,000 patch memories, 800 of them preset.

instruments.name: Octave Kitten
instruments.text: A cut-down CAT with one oscillator and two sub-oscillator options, one and two octaves down.

instruments.name: Octave-Plateau Voyetra Eight
instruments.text: An eight-voice programmable analogue polysynth in a 19-inch rack, with two VCOs and a 24 dB/octave resonant low-pass filter per voice, 100 programs and split and layer modes, played from MIDI or the optional VPK-5 keyboard.

instruments.name: OSC OSCar
instruments.text: A monophonic synthesiser with limited duophony, two digital oscillators with additive harmonic editing, two combinable analogue filters, a 37-key keyboard, MIDI and a rubberised case.

instruments.name: PAiA 2720
instruments.text: PAiA's first modular synthesizer series, sold as kits and published in Radio-Electronics, using Hz/V rather than V/octave pitch control.

instruments.name: PAiA 4700
instruments.text: PAiA's second modular synthesizer system, which could be placed under computer control by the 8700 controller.

instruments.name: PAiA Proteus 1
instruments.text: A kit-built monophonic synthesizer of which only about 70 to 80 were produced.

instruments.name: PAiA Stringz 'n' Things
instruments.text: A string synthesizer from PAiA's range of electronic instrument kits.

instruments.name: PAiA FatMan
instruments.text: A MIDI-capable monophonic analogue synthesizer.

instruments.name: PAiA 9700
instruments.text: PAiA's later modular synthesizer line.

instruments.name: Peavey DPM 3
instruments.text: Peavey's first synthesiser, a 16-voice sample-plus-synthesis workstation with two oscillators per voice, a sequencer, effects and a velocity- and aftertouch-sensitive five-octave keyboard.

instruments.name: Peavey DPM SP
instruments.text: A dedicated sample-playback synthesiser module, partnered by the DPM SX sample input unit.

instruments.name: Peavey Spectrum Bass
instruments.text: A 1U rack bass module with 200 preset bass sounds, eight-voice polyphony and four-part multitimbrality, using synthesis from the DPM series.

instruments.name: Pittsburgh Modular Lifeforms SV-1 Blackbox
instruments.text: A desktop analogue semi-modular with two oscillators with sub-octaves, noise, a state-variable filter, ADSR, VCA, MIDI-to-CV with LFOs and about 53 patch points over normalled routing.

instruments.name: Pittsburgh Modular Microvolt 3900
instruments.text: A desktop analogue semi-modular monosynth with one wave-shaping oscillator, a two-pole low-pass filter with a self-resonating mode, an arpeggiator and optional patch cables.

instruments.name: Pittsburgh Modular Voltage Research Laboratory
instruments.text: A West Coast-inspired analogue modular workstation of three Eurorack modules (a voice, a touch controller and an output utility) in one handmade case, funded on Kickstarter.

instruments.name: Pittsburgh Modular Taiga
instruments.text: A three-oscillator paraphonic analogue semi-modular that works standalone or as a 60hp Eurorack panel, with wave-shaping oscillators, a multimode filter and a Dynamics Controller, later also made in a keyboard version.

instruments.name: Pittsburgh Modular Voltage Lab 2
instruments.text: A standalone dual-oscillator analogue modular synth succeeding the Voltage Research Laboratory, with wave-shaping Laboratory Oscillators, a low-pass-gate Dynamics Controller, a touch controller, effects and a chance sequencer.

instruments.name: Polyend Medusa
instruments.text: A hybrid synth made with Dreadbox, with three analogue and three digital wavetable oscillators, mono and three- or six-note paraphonic modes through a shared filter, played and sequenced from a pad grid.

instruments.name: Polyend Synth
instruments.text: An eight-voice digital synthesizer that runs three of its eight engines at once, played from an RGB pad grid with polyphonic aftertouch and three 64-step sequencers.

instruments.name: Polyfusion Series 2000
instruments.text: A large-format modular synthesiser built by former Moog Music staff Ron Folkman and Alan Pearce as a successor to the Moog modular system.

instruments.name: PPG 300 Series
instruments.text: An analogue modular synthesizer, Wolfgang Palm's first commercially available instrument.

instruments.name: PPG 1003 Sonic Carrier
instruments.text: A duophonic digital synthesizer, the first PPG instrument with sound storage.

instruments.name: PPG 1002
instruments.text: A portable monophonic analogue synthesizer with voltage-controlled oscillators.

instruments.name: PPG 1020
instruments.text: A portable monophonic analogue synthesizer with digitally controlled oscillators.

instruments.name: PPG 340/380 System
instruments.text: A digital synthesizer workstation of processor and generator units with a 16-track sequencer and a computer terminal with monitor, 8-inch floppy drives and a five-octave keyboard.

instruments.name: PPG Wave Computer 360
instruments.text: An eight-voice polyphonic digital synthesizer with analogue filters and VCAs, of which about 40 were made.

instruments.name: PPG Wave 2.2
instruments.text: The successor to the Wave 2, a hybrid wavetable synthesizer with two oscillators per voice, analogue filters and an integrated sequencer.

instruments.name: PPG EVU
instruments.text: An eight-voice expander version of the Wave synthesizers, the Expansion Voice Unit.

instruments.name: PPG Wave 2.3
instruments.text: A hybrid wavetable synthesizer whose voices can each play a different sound, with resolution raised from 8 to 12 bits and MIDI added.

instruments.name: Quasimidi Quasar
instruments.text: A rack synthesiser combining sample-plus-synthesis, FM and additive methods, with built-in effects in a 2U rack case.

instruments.name: Quasimidi Raven
instruments.text: A full-size sample-based virtual analogue keyboard synthesiser with a sequencer for muting and transposing tracks, expandable with the MAXX board.

instruments.name: Quasimidi Technox
instruments.text: A synthesiser module from Quasimidi's mid-1990s range.

instruments.name: Quasimidi Polymorph
instruments.text: The successor to the Rave-O-Lution and Quasimidi's last product before the company closed in 2000.

instruments.name: Moog Synthesizer I
instruments.text: The smallest of Moog's first-generation modular systems, sold as the 1C in a single studio cabinet or the 1P in a portable suitcase.

instruments.name: Moog Synthesizer II
instruments.text: The mid-sized first-generation Moog modular system, sold in console (2C) and portable (2P) versions.

instruments.name: Moog Synthesizer III
instruments.text: The largest first-generation Moog modular system, fully implemented with first-generation modules and sold in console (3C) and portable (3P) versions.

instruments.name: Moog Model 10
instruments.text: The smallest Moog modular, in a single suitcase, built from eleven modules including three 900-series oscillators, a lowpass filter, the 907 fixed filter bank and two envelope generators.

instruments.name: Realistic Concertmate MG-1
instruments.text: Built by Moog Music for Radio Shack: two monophonic oscillators with sync plus a divide-down polyphonic square-wave section through one filter, on a 32-key keyboard; about 23,000 were sold in 1982–83, more than any other synthesizer Moog Music made.

instruments.name: Rhodes Model 760
instruments.text: A 76-key sample-playback synthesizer built by Roland on the U-20 engine under the Rhodes name, also sold with 61 keys as the Model 660.

instruments.name: Rhodes Chroma Polaris
instruments.text: A six-voice analogue polysynth with two DCOs per voice, a 24 dB filter, 132 sounds, a polyphonic sequencer, MIDI and a five-octave keyboard, as a cheaper follow-up to the Chroma.

instruments.name: Roland SH-1000
instruments.text: Roland's first synthesiser and the first compact synthesiser produced in Japan, an analogue monosynth with one VCO plus sub-oscillator tabs, a resonant low-pass filter, ten presets and a 37-key keyboard.

instruments.name: Roland SH-2000
instruments.text: A preset-only analogue monosynth with one VCO and aftertouch, using a Hz/V control standard unlike Roland's other models.

instruments.name: Roland SH-3
instruments.text: An analogue monosynth with one VCO using additive-style oscillation for its distinctive sound, also sold in revised form as the SH-3A.

instruments.name: Roland RS-101
instruments.text: Roland's string synthesiser released in 1975 and succeeded by the RS-202.

instruments.name: Roland SH-5
instruments.text: Roland's first two-VCO analogue synthesiser, and the first Roland synth to have pitch-bender levers.

instruments.name: Roland RS-202
instruments.text: A string synthesiser with divide-down sawtooth oscillators giving full polyphony across a five-octave keyboard, a single shared envelope, separate sounds for the top and bottom of the keyboard and an analogue-delay chorus ensemble.

instruments.name: Roland RS-505 Paraphonic
instruments.text: A paraphonic analogue keyboard with three tone sections (strings, polysynth and bass) on a 49-key keyboard split down the middle.

instruments.name: Roland SH-1
instruments.text: A one-VCO analogue monosynth in a moulded plastic case, the first Roland synth to include a sub-oscillator.

instruments.name: Roland SH-7
instruments.text: A two-VCO analogue synthesiser in a smaller case, the successor to the SH-5, able to play two voices.

instruments.name: Roland System-100M
instruments.text: A compact, consumer-oriented modular synthesiser system derived from the System-700, offered with 32- or 49-key keyboards.

instruments.name: Roland Promars
instruments.text: A monophonic version of the Jupiter-4 with two VCOs, eight user memories and ten presets.

instruments.name: Roland Juno-6
instruments.text: A six-voice analogue polysynth with one DCO per voice, a built-in chorus and key transpose.

instruments.name: Roland MKS-30
instruments.text: A 2U rack version of the JX-3P analogue polysynth with programmable MIDI channels.

instruments.name: Roland MKS-80 Super Jupiter
instruments.text: An eight-voice analogue polysynth in a 2U rack, nicknamed the Super Jupiter, with an optional MPG-80 programmer.

instruments.name: Roland MKS-7 Super Quartet
instruments.text: A rack unit combining a duophonic lead synth, a monophonic bass synth and a four-voice synth with a drum section of 11 PCM sounds from the TR-707.

instruments.name: Roland JX-10 Super JX
instruments.text: A 76-key analogue polysynth built from two JX-8P sound generators for 12-voice polyphony, nicknamed the Super JX, with an optional PG-800 programmer.

instruments.name: Roland MKS-50
instruments.text: A rack-mounted version of the Alpha Juno that adds portamento, detune and chord memory, programmable with the optional PG-300.

instruments.name: Roland MKS-70
instruments.text: A rack version of the JX-10, programmable with the same PG-800 programmer, with portamento, delay and chorus effects.

instruments.name: Roland D-50
instruments.text: Roland's first fully digital synthesiser, a 16-voice keyboard using Linear Arithmetic synthesis that combines sampled attack transients with subtractive synthesis, with on-board digital effects and a joystick.

instruments.name: Roland D-550
instruments.text: The rack-mount version of the D-50, with the same Linear Arithmetic sound circuitry, editable with the PG-1000 external programmer.

instruments.name: Roland MT-32
instruments.text: A Linear Arithmetic synthesiser module with 32 partials, eight melodic parts and a rhythm part, which became an early standard for computer game music.

instruments.name: Roland D-10
instruments.text: A multitimbral digital keyboard with the D-50's Linear Arithmetic sound generator, a built-in rhythm section and digital reverb.

instruments.name: Roland D-110
instruments.text: The D-10's Linear Arithmetic sound generator in a 1U rack, with six individual outputs plus a stereo main output.

instruments.name: Roland D-20
instruments.text: A Linear Arithmetic synthesiser with the D-10's features plus a nine-track sequencer and a 3.5-inch floppy drive.

instruments.name: Roland U-110
instruments.text: A PCM sample-playback sound module covering a wide range of instrument tones, with slots for up to four memory cards.

instruments.name: Roland D-5
instruments.text: A budget Linear Arithmetic synthesiser with a chase function and an arpeggiator.

instruments.name: Roland U-20
instruments.text: A PCM sample-playback keyboard using the RS-PCM sound generator, compatible with U-110 tone data.

instruments.name: Roland U-220
instruments.text: An RS-PCM sample-playback module above the U-110, with 128 preset tones and built-in chorus and reverb.

instruments.name: Roland W-30
instruments.text: A 61-key sampling workstation with a 12-bit sampler, 16-voice polyphony and a 16-track sequencer, compatible with Roland's S-50 and S-550 sample libraries.

instruments.name: Roland D-70
instruments.text: A 76-key synthesiser using Advanced LA synthesis, a development of Linear Arithmetic synthesis, with a DLM function for generating wave data.

instruments.name: Roland JD-800
instruments.text: A digital synthesiser with a large number of sliders for real-time parameter control and up to four tones per patch.

instruments.name: Roland JX-1
instruments.text: A low-priced keyboard built around preset sounds, with an eight-parameter edit function.

instruments.name: Roland JV-30
instruments.text: A 16-part multitimbral PCM synthesiser below the JV-80, with 189 built-in tones and filter, envelope and vibrato editing.

instruments.name: Roland JV-80
instruments.text: A PCM synthesiser with eight parameter sliders, the first synth compatible with the SR-JV80 series of expansion boards.

instruments.name: Roland JV-880
instruments.text: A 1U rack PCM module with the JV-80's sounds and functions, four outputs and a preview function.

instruments.name: Roland JW-50
instruments.text: A workstation with a GS sound generator and a 16-track sequencer, with a backing function and simplified tone editing.

instruments.name: Roland JD-990
instruments.text: A rack sound module developed from the JD-800, with a large display, ring modulation, oscillator sync, FXM and eight multi-effects.

instruments.name: Roland JV-1000
instruments.text: A workstation combining a refined JV-80 sound generator with an MC-50MKII sequencer, expandable to 993 patches and 56 voices.

instruments.name: Roland JV-35
instruments.text: An expandable synthesiser keyboard that takes boards for extra sounds and voices.

instruments.name: Roland JV-50
instruments.text: The JV-35 with a built-in Standard MIDI File player added, expandable to 56 voices.

instruments.name: Roland JV-90
instruments.text: A PCM synthesiser equivalent to the JV-1000 without its sequencer, expandable with boards that add voices and sounds.

instruments.name: Roland XP-10
instruments.text: An affordable 16-part multitimbral GM/GS synthesiser with a 30-style arpeggiator and Combination Palette.

instruments.name: Roland XP-50
instruments.text: A workstation with the JV-1080 sound generator, a loop-recording sequencer and Realtime Phrase Sequence.

instruments.name: Roland JP-8000
instruments.text: An eight-voice analogue-modelling synthesiser with a large array of knobs and sliders and Motion Control for recording and playing back panel moves.

instruments.name: Roland XP-80
instruments.text: The top XP-series workstation, based on the XP-50 with a 76-key weighted keyboard and a larger sequencer, later also sold as the 61-key XP-60.

instruments.name: Roland JV-2080
instruments.text: A sample-playback sound module with 640 patches and 16 multitimbral parts.

instruments.name: Roland JP-8080
instruments.text: A rack version of the JP-8000 analogue-modelling synth with 10-voice polyphony, Unison, a Voice Modulator and an external audio input.

instruments.name: Roland JV-1010
instruments.text: A compact half-rack module with sounds from the JV-1080 and JV-2080 and a slot for one SR-JV80 expansion board.

instruments.name: Roland XP-30
instruments.text: The last XP-series synthesiser, without a sequencer, with 1,406 patches and an arpeggiator.

instruments.name: Roland RS-5
instruments.text: An affordable synthesiser with sounds from the JV, XP and XV series and knobs for LFO, filter and other parameters.

instruments.name: Roland XV-3080
instruments.text: A 2U rack module with the XV-88's sound generator, holding two SRX and four SR-JV80 expansion boards.

instruments.name: Roland XV-5080
instruments.text: The top XV-series rack module, with Matrix Control and sample playback from SIMM memory.

instruments.name: Roland XV-88
instruments.text: A 128-voice synthesiser with an 88-key hammer-action keyboard and slots for two SRX and two SR-JV80 expansion boards.

instruments.name: Roland Fantom
instruments.text: A 76-key workstation with a large graphical LCD and sound quality from the XV-5080.

instruments.name: Roland SH-32
instruments.text: A synthesiser that revived the SH prefix after 20 years, with a traditional panel layout and a programmable arpeggiator.

instruments.name: Roland XV-5050
instruments.text: A 64-voice, 16-part 1U rack module with XV-5080 sound quality, supplied with editing software.

instruments.name: Roland XV-2020
instruments.text: A half-rack XV-series module with USB, GM2 compatibility, 16 parts, three effects processors and two SRX expansion slots.

instruments.name: Roland Fantom-S
instruments.text: A 61-note workstation integrating audio and MIDI, with sampling, real-time time-stretching, Skip Back Sampling and a pad bank.

instruments.name: Roland RS-50
instruments.text: A scaled-down RS-70 for live performance, with a phrase and arpeggio generator and multi chord memory.

instruments.name: Roland RS-70
instruments.text: A live-performance synthesiser with a loop sequencer and direct-access buttons.

instruments.name: Roland V-Synth
instruments.text: A 61-key, 24-voice synthesiser combining VariPhrase real-time control of waveform pitch, time and formant with analogue-modelling oscillators, COSM filters, a sampler and a Time Trip pad.

instruments.name: Roland VariOS
instruments.text: A hardware/software sound module system built on VariPhrase, later expanded with VariOS-8 and VariOS 303 software emulating Roland's Juno, Jupiter and TB-303.

instruments.name: Roland Fantom-X
instruments.text: A workstation with 128-voice polyphony, nearly 1GB of wave memory when expanded with four SRX cards, eight stereo audio tracks and a large colour LCD.

instruments.name: Roland Fantom-Xa
instruments.text: A lower-cost sampling workstation in the Fantom-X family with a 16-track sequencer.

instruments.name: Roland Fantom-XR
instruments.text: A 1U rack module version of the Fantom-X, holding over 1GB of sounds with six SRX cards and memory upgrades.

instruments.name: Roland Juno-D
instruments.text: A budget PCM synthesiser with 640 patches, multi-effects, real-time controllers and groove tools.

instruments.name: Roland V-Synth XT
instruments.text: A rack-mount version of the V-Synth without its D Beams and Time Trip pad.

instruments.name: Roland Juno-G
instruments.text: A 128-voice PCM synthesiser with a Fantom-X-class engine, SRX expansion and a 16-part MIDI sequencer with four stereo audio tracks.

instruments.name: Roland SH-201
instruments.text: A 49-key analogue-modelling synthesiser with Roland's Super Saw waveform, an external audio input, D Beam and real-time knobs and switches.

instruments.name: Roland SonicCell
instruments.text: A desktop sound module with two SRX expansion bays, a built-in USB audio interface and audio file playback.

instruments.name: Roland V-Synth GT
instruments.text: A 28-voice dual-engine V-Synth with Elastic Audio Synthesis, Articulative Phrase Synthesis for modelling acoustic instrument performance, and Vocal Designer.

instruments.name: Roland Fantom-G
instruments.text: A workstation sold in 61-, 76- and 88-key sizes (Fantom-G6, G7, G8) with ARX SuperNATURAL expansion, a large colour LCD and a 152-track audio/MIDI sequencer.

instruments.name: Roland Juno-Stage
instruments.text: A 76-key performance synthesiser with a large display, USB backing-track playback, a click output and performance knobs.

instruments.name: Roland AX-Synth
instruments.text: A battery-powered 49-key shoulder keyboard with an on-board sound generator built around solo-oriented sounds.

instruments.name: Roland Juno-Di
instruments.text: A lightweight, battery-powered PCM synthesiser with more than 1,000 sounds and a song player.

instruments.name: Roland GAIA SH-01
instruments.text: An affordable synthesiser with a triple-stacked engine and hands-on controls.

instruments.name: Roland Juno-Gi
instruments.text: A PCM synthesiser with more than 1,300 sounds, an eight-track digital recorder and BOSS effects.

instruments.name: Roland Lucina AX-09
instruments.text: A light 37-key shoulder synthesiser with 150 sounds, category buttons and a USB audio player.

instruments.name: Roland Jupiter-80
instruments.text: A live-performance synthesiser built on Roland's SuperNATURAL sound technology, named after the Jupiter-8.

instruments.name: Roland INTEGRA-7
instruments.text: A rack sound module collecting sounds from Roland's flagship keyboards and V-Drums modules plus the SRX library, with a 17-part Motional Surround ambience engine.

instruments.name: Roland Jupiter-50
instruments.text: A more portable SuperNATURAL synthesiser combining the Jupiter-80's sound with the size of the Juno series.

instruments.name: Roland FA-06
instruments.text: A music workstation with the INTEGRA-7 sound collection and studio effects, also sold as the 88-key weighted FA-08 and later the 76-key FA-07.

instruments.name: Roland SYSTEM-1
instruments.text: An AIRA synthesiser using ACB circuit modelling that can also host PLUG-OUT software recreations of Roland synths without a computer.

instruments.name: Roland TB-3 Touch Bassline
instruments.text: An AIRA bass synth drawn from the TB-303 design, using ACB circuit modelling and played and programmed from a pressure-sensitive touch pad.

instruments.name: Roland Boutique JP-08
instruments.text: A four-voice Boutique module recreating the Jupiter-8 with ACB circuit modelling, with extra LFOs and an expanded VCO range.

instruments.name: Roland Boutique JU-06
instruments.text: A four-voice Boutique module recreating the Juno-106 with ACB circuit modelling, including its chorus, a faster LFO and a continuously variable high-pass filter.

instruments.name: Roland Boutique JX-03
instruments.text: A four-voice Boutique module recreating the JX-3P with ACB circuit modelling, adding new waveforms, an expanded DCO range and cross-modulation.

instruments.name: Roland JD-XA
instruments.text: A crossover synthesiser pairing a four-part discrete analogue engine (two oscillators and an analogue filter per part) with a four-part, 64-voice SuperNATURAL digital engine whose sounds can pass through the analogue filters.

instruments.name: Roland JD-Xi
instruments.text: A 37-mini-key crossover synthesiser with one analogue synth part and two 128-voice SuperNATURAL digital parts, drum kits, a four-track pattern sequencer and a vocoder with gooseneck microphone.

instruments.name: Roland Juno-DS
instruments.text: A performance synthesiser in 61- and 88-key versions carrying the Juno-Di's 1,000-plus sounds, with waveform expansion, eight phrase pads, a pattern sequencer and a vocoder.

instruments.name: Roland SYSTEM-1m
instruments.text: A semi-modular AIRA synthesiser with PLUG-OUT capability and CV/gate patching, usable as a Eurorack module, a tabletop synth or a 19-inch rack unit.

instruments.name: Roland Boutique TB-03
instruments.text: A Boutique bass line synth recreating the TB-303 with ACB circuit modelling, with saw and square waves, a four-digit LED display, effects and CV/gate.

instruments.name: Roland Boutique VP-03
instruments.text: A Boutique vocoder module recreating the VP-330, with vocoder, human voice and string sound sources, chord memory and a voice step sequencer.

instruments.name: Roland SYSTEM-500 Complete Set
instruments.text: An analogue Eurorack modular system of five modules giving two VCOs, two VCFs, two VCAs, two envelopes with an LFO, and a phase shifter and delay module.

instruments.name: Roland SYSTEM-8
instruments.text: A 49-key AIRA synthesiser using ACB circuit modelling that hosts up to three PLUG-OUT synths, with a polyphonic step sequencer, arpeggiator, vocoder and CV/gate outputs.

instruments.name: Roland Boutique D-05
instruments.text: A 16-voice Boutique module recreating the D-50's Linear Arithmetic synthesis, with the original presets, a joystick, a sequencer and an arpeggiator.

instruments.name: Roland Boutique SE-02
instruments.text: An analogue synth module made with Studio Electronics, with discrete circuitry, three VCOs, a 24dB low-pass filter, cross-modulation, 384 presets and a 16-step sequencer.

instruments.name: Roland Boutique SH-01A
instruments.text: A four-voice Boutique module reproducing the SH-101 with ACB circuit modelling, with mono, poly, unison and chord modes and a 100-step sequencer.

instruments.name: Roland AX-Edge
instruments.text: A 49-key keytar synthesiser with a stage-oriented sound set, a built-in vocoder, an arpeggiator and interchangeable blades.

instruments.name: Roland Boutique JU-06A
instruments.text: A Boutique module combining the sound and features of the Juno-60 and Juno-106, including the 106's high-pass filter, the 60's envelope-controlled pulse-width modulation and the Juno chorus, with a sequencer and arpeggiator.

instruments.name: Roland Fantom 6
instruments.text: A 16-part synthesiser workstation sold in 61-, 76- and 88-key sizes (Fantom 6, 7, 8), with a colour touchscreen, modeless Scenes and CV/gate outputs.

instruments.name: Roland Jupiter-Xm
instruments.text: A 37-key battery-capable synthesiser with four synth parts and a drum part, models of Roland synths and drum machines, and the I-Arpeggio function.

instruments.name: Roland Jupiter-X
instruments.text: A 61-key synthesiser with four synth parts and a drum part, models of Roland synths, the XV-5080 and drum machines, and the I-Arpeggio function.

instruments.name: Roland AIRA Compact J-6
instruments.text: A pocket chord synthesiser using the Juno-60 sound engine, with 100 chord sets, filter, envelope, delay and reverb.

instruments.name: Roland Boutique JD-08
instruments.text: A Boutique module recreating the JD-800's four-tone structure, 108 waveforms and multi-effects, with expanded polyphony and a two-part polyphonic sequencer.

instruments.name: Roland Boutique JX-08
instruments.text: A Boutique module based on the JX-8P with expanded polyphony, two-part multitimbrality, the original's 32 presets and a polyphonic sequencer.

instruments.name: Roland Fantom-06
instruments.text: A streamlined Fantom workstation with ZEN-Core, SuperNATURAL and Virtual ToneWheel organ engines, a colour touchscreen and a clip sequencer, also sold as the 76-key Fantom-07 and 88-key Fantom-08.

instruments.name: Roland Juno-X
instruments.text: A 61-key ZEN-Core synthesiser with models of the Juno-60 and Juno-106, the XV-5080 and a vocoder, up to four layered tones and the I-Arpeggio function.

instruments.name: Roland AIRA Compact S-1
instruments.text: A four-voice pocket polysynth using ACB circuit modelling, inspired by the SH-101.

instruments.name: Roland GAIA 2
instruments.text: A 37-key synthesiser with a wavetable oscillator and two virtual-analogue oscillators, Model Expansion support, a Motional Pad and a sequencer.

instruments.name: Roland SH-4d
instruments.text: A desktop synthesiser with 11 oscillator models, 60-note polyphony, a four-part multitimbral sequencer with a rhythm part, and motion sensors.

instruments.name: Roland Juno-D6
instruments.text: A ZEN-Core synthesiser with over 3,800 sounds, an eight-track sequencer, phrase pads and an arpeggiator, also sold as the 76-key Juno-D7 and 88-key Juno-D8.

instruments.name: RSF PolyKobol
instruments.text: An eight-voice analogue polysynth with two VCOs per voice, 32 memories, an eight-track sequencer and onboard tape storage, of which only 30 were made.

instruments.name: Sequential Prophet X
instruments.text: A bi-timbral hybrid synthesiser, eight voices in stereo or sixteen in mono, combining two sample-based instruments and two digital oscillators per voice through analogue filters, with a five-octave keyboard.

instruments.name: Sequential Pro 3
instruments.text: A hybrid monosynth, three-voice paraphonic on demand, with two VCOs and a wavetable oscillator, a choice of three analogue filters (Prophet-6, ladder and OB-6 state-variable) and a 16-track sequencer.

instruments.name: Sequential Prophet-10
instruments.text: A ten-voice version of the 2020 Prophet-5 Rev4, bi-timbral for layers and splits, reintroducing the Prophet-10 in the Prophet-5's single-keyboard case.

instruments.name: Sequential Prophet-5 Rev4
instruments.text: A five-voice analogue polysynth with two VCOs per voice and switchable filters from the earlier revisions, made by Sequential as a recreation of the original Prophet-5.

instruments.name: Sequential Take 5
instruments.text: A compact five-voice analogue polysynth with two VCOs and a sub-oscillator per voice, the 4-pole filter from the Prophet-5 Rev4 and 44 keys.

instruments.name: Sequential Trigon-6
instruments.text: A six-voice analogue polysynth with three VCOs per voice and a 2- or 4-pole ladder filter, the last design Dave Smith contributed to.

instruments.name: Sequential Fourm
instruments.text: A compact four-voice analogue polysynth with two oscillators and a 4-pole low-pass filter per voice derived from the Prophet-5, on a slim-key keyboard with polyphonic aftertouch.

instruments.name: Sequential Circuits Prophet-10
instruments.text: A ten-voice analogue polysynth with 20 oscillators and a double keyboard, built as the larger sibling of the Prophet-5.

instruments.name: Sequential Circuits Prophet-T8
instruments.text: An eight-voice analogue polysynth with two VCOs per voice, a self-oscillating filter, MIDI and a 76-key weighted wooden keyboard with velocity and polyphonic aftertouch.

instruments.name: Sequential Circuits Max
instruments.text: A six-voice multitimbral analogue synthesiser with a four-octave keyboard and a six-track recorder, designed as a MIDI voice expander for computer-based setups.

instruments.name: Sequential Circuits Multi-Trak
instruments.text: A six-voice multitimbral analogue polysynth with one VCO per voice, a five-octave velocity-sensitive keyboard, a built-in real-time sequencer, a programmable chorus and an arpeggiator.

instruments.name: Sequential Circuits Prophet 2000
instruments.text: An eight-voice 12-bit sampling keyboard with 61 keys and eight analogue filters, later joined by the rack-mounted Prophet 2002.

instruments.name: Sequential Circuits Split-Eight
instruments.text: An eight-voice bi-timbral analogue polysynth built around the Curtis CEM 3394 synth-on-a-chip, with a 61-key keyboard that can split or layer two sounds, sold in some markets as the Pro-8.

instruments.name: Siel Mono
instruments.text: A simple monophonic synthesiser with one DCO and one VCF.

instruments.name: Siel Cruise
instruments.text: A hybrid combining the Siel Mono synthesiser with the divide-down polyphonic Orchestra in one keyboard.

instruments.name: Siel Orchestra 2
instruments.text: An improved Orchestra (OR400) with more parameter sliders, which Sequential Circuits sold as the Prelude.

instruments.name: Siel Opera 6
instruments.text: A six-voice analogue polysynth with two oscillators per voice, 100 memories and a velocity-sensitive five-octave keyboard with MIDI.

instruments.name: Siel DK600
instruments.text: The Opera 6 in different styling, with a later EPROM adding MIDI channel and Omni-off support.

instruments.name: Siel Expander
instruments.text: A tabletop module version of the Opera 6 and DK600.

instruments.name: Siel DK70
instruments.text: One half of the DK80, using eight DCOs as eight single-oscillator voices or four two-oscillator voices, also sold as the Giannini GS 7010.

instruments.name: Siel DK80
instruments.text: A polysynth that can split or layer two six-voice synthesisers.

instruments.name: Siel Expander 80
instruments.text: The DK80 in module form.

instruments.name: Siel DK700
instruments.text: An enhanced DK600 with digital parameter editing in place of knobs.

instruments.name: SOMA Laboratory Lyra-8
instruments.text: An eight-voice analogue "organismic" synthesizer whose individually tuned voices are played from touch pads and modulate one another, with a modulation delay and distortion and no keyboard.

instruments.name: Sonicware Liven 8bit Warps
instruments.text: A portable 27-key 8-bit wave-memory synthesizer with four engines, filters, effects, a 64-step sequencer and a built-in speaker.

instruments.name: Sonicware Liven XFM
instruments.text: A portable 27-key four-operator FM synthesizer with six-note polyphony, three fused-FM engines and a four-track sequencer.

instruments.name: Sonicware Liven Ambient Ø
instruments.text: A portable ambient synthesizer with four mixable layers (drone, pads, atmos and noise), up to ten voices, a per-layer 64-step sequencer and several reverbs and delays.

instruments.name: Sonicware Liven Evoke
instruments.text: A portable synth whose oscillator is built from sliced recordings of 34 acoustic instruments, with a harmonic sub-oscillator, granular effects, a chord engine and a four-track sequencer.

instruments.name: Steiner-Parker Synthacon
instruments.text: A monophonic analogue synthesiser from Salt Lake City with three VCOs, a 12dB/octave multimode filter and a 49-key keyboard, using the same circuitry as Steiner-Parker's SynthaSystem modular.

instruments.name: Steiner-Parker Microcon
instruments.text: A smaller version of the Synthacon, developed for the Swede Patch 2000 guitar synthesiser.

instruments.name: Studio Electronics Midimini
instruments.text: A rackmounted three-oscillator monosynth built as a Minimoog in rack form with MIDI.

instruments.name: Studio Electronics SE-1
instruments.text: A 3U rack analogue monosynth under digital control with three oscillators, licensed Moog circuitry, a 24dB/12dB resonant filter and 99 memories, described as the first new analogue monosynth since 1984.

instruments.name: Studio Electronics ATC-1
instruments.text: A 2U rack analogue monosynth with two VCOs and plug-in filter cartridges modelled on the Minimoog, TB-303, Oberheim SEM and ARP 2600 filters.

instruments.name: Studio Electronics SE-1X
instruments.text: An updated version of the SE-1 rackmounted analogue monosynth.

instruments.name: Studio Electronics Omega 8
instruments.text: An eight-voice digitally controlled analogue rack polysynth with two oscillators, a filter and an amplifier per voice, a multitimbral mode and many front-panel knobs.

instruments.name: Studio Electronics ATC-X
instruments.text: A 2U rack analogue monosynth with two oscillators and four built-in selectable filters modelled on the Minimoog, Oberheim SEM, TB-303 and ARP 2600, plus distortion and a ring modulator.

instruments.name: Studio Electronics Boomstar 3003
instruments.text: A desktop analogue monosynth with two VCOs, two hardware envelopes and a 24dB filter modelled on the Roland TB-303's.

instruments.name: Studio Electronics Boomstar 4075
instruments.text: A desktop analogue monosynth with two VCOs, two hardware envelopes and a 24dB filter modelled on the ARP 2600's.

instruments.name: Studio Electronics Boomstar 5089
instruments.text: A desktop analogue monosynth with two VCOs, two hardware envelopes and a 24dB ladder filter modelled on the Minimoog's.

instruments.name: Studio Electronics Boomstar SEM
instruments.text: A desktop analogue monosynth with two VCOs, two hardware envelopes and a 12dB multi-mode filter modelled on the Oberheim SEM's.

instruments.name: Studio Electronics Midimini V30
instruments.text: A 30th-anniversary return of the Midimini as a 4U rack analogue monosynth on a three-oscillator Minimoog-style core, adding an LFO, ring modulation, overdrive and CV patch points.

instruments.name: Studio Electronics SE-3X
instruments.text: A three-oscillator rack synth developed from the SE-1X that plays mono or three-note paraphonic, with four switchable analogue filters modelled on Moog, ARP, Roland and Oberheim designs.

instruments.name: Synclavier Regen
instruments.text: A desktop digital synthesizer built on an enhanced Synclavier II DSP engine, with 12 partials per sound, additive and subtractive synthesis, sample playback and resynthesis.

instruments.name: Synton Syrinx
instruments.text: A monophonic analogue synthesiser made in a small run across 1983 and 1984.

instruments.name: Synton Fénix
instruments.text: An analogue modular synthesiser built by former Synton staff Marc Paping and Bert Vermeulen, made in a run of 75 units until 2000.

instruments.name: Technics SX-WSA1
instruments.text: A 64-note polyphonic acoustic-modelling synthesiser that pairs PCM drivers with modelled resonators, with a 61-note velocity- and pressure-sensitive keyboard and a 16-track sequencer.

instruments.name: Technics SX-WSA1R
instruments.text: The rack module version of the WSA1, with 64-voice polyphony and 32-part multitimbrality.

instruments.name: Teenage Engineering OP-1
instruments.text: A portable six-voice digital synthesizer, sampler and sequencer with eleven synthesis engines including FM, a 24-key keyboard and a built-in tape recorder, first shown as a prototype at NAMM 2010.

instruments.name: Teenage Engineering PO-14 Sub
instruments.text: A credit-card-sized Pocket Operator bass-line synthesizer with a built-in sequencer, launched with the first three Pocket Operators.

instruments.name: Teenage Engineering PO-16 Factory
instruments.text: A credit-card-sized Pocket Operator lead synthesizer for key melodies, played from its own sequencer.

instruments.name: Teenage Engineering PO-20 Arcade
instruments.text: A credit-card-sized Pocket Operator synthesizer and sequencer with arcade-game sounds.

instruments.name: Teenage Engineering PO-28 Robot
instruments.text: A credit-card-sized Pocket Operator synthesizer and sequencer designed for live playing.

instruments.name: Teenage Engineering OP-Z
instruments.text: A screenless 16-track synthesizer and sequencer with several synth engines, sample tracks and two octaves of pressure-sensitive keys, edited through a phone or tablet app and able to sequence lights and visuals.

instruments.name: Teenage Engineering Pocket Operator Modular 170
instruments.text: A flat-pack monophonic analogue modular synthesizer kit with nine modules, a built-in keyboard, a programmable sequencer and a speaker box, using ±12 volt modules and 3.5mm patch cables.

instruments.name: Teenage Engineering Pocket Operator Modular 400
instruments.text: The largest flat-pack analogue modular kit of the series, with three oscillators, noise, a mixer, random generator, two envelopes, two VCAs, an LFO, a 16-step sequencer and 16 modules in all.

instruments.name: Teenage Engineering OP-1 field
instruments.text: The successor to the OP-1, with a fully stereo 32-bit signal path, a four-track stereo tape recorder with several tape modes, Bluetooth MIDI and a new Dimension synth engine beside the original engines.

instruments.name: Teenage Engineering OP-XY
instruments.text: A portable 24-voice synthesizer, sampler and 64-step sequencer with multiple stereo synth engines, a small keyboard, eight instrument tracks and a built-in speaker, positioned as the successor to the OP-Z.

instruments.name: Teisco S-100F
instruments.text: Kawai's first synthesizer, sold under the revived Teisco name: a monophonic analogue synth with one VCO, a 24dB resonant low-pass filter, a manual high-pass filter, two envelopes and a three-octave keyboard.

instruments.name: Teisco S-100P
instruments.text: A monophonic analogue preset synth with a 37-key aftertouch keyboard, 32 presets, one VCO, a 24dB low-pass filter, spring reverb and portamento and glissando, also sold as the Kawai S-100P.

instruments.name: Teisco S-110F
instruments.text: A duophonic analogue synth in a wedge-shaped case with two independently playable oscillators offering triangle, sawtooth and variable pulse waves, sample-and-hold and a fixed eight-band filter bank.

instruments.name: Teisco S-60F
instruments.text: A one-oscillator monophonic analogue synth, the smaller companion to the S-110F.

instruments.name: Teisco SX-400
instruments.text: A four-voice analogue polysynth with one VCO and sub-oscillator per voice, a 24dB low-pass filter plus high-pass filter, two ADSR envelopes, a four-octave pressure-sensitive keyboard and eight preset and eight user memories.

instruments.name: Telefunken Trautonium Ela T 42
instruments.text: A monophonic Trautonium sold for home music, with a glow-lamp sawtooth oscillator played by pressing a resistance wire against a metal rail, of which about 200 were made.

instruments.name: Tom Oberheim SEM
instruments.text: A new production of the Synthesizer Expander Module, manufactured by Marion Systems and branded tomoberheim.com while Gibson held the Oberheim trademark.

instruments.name: Tom Oberheim Two Voice Pro
instruments.text: A two-voice SEM-based synthesiser manufactured by Marion Systems and branded tomoberheim.com.

instruments.name: Twisted Electrons TherapSid
instruments.text: A desktop synth built around the Commodore SID chip, with three oscillators, a multimode filter, three LFOs, a 16-step modulator and 100 presets.

instruments.name: Twisted Electrons AY3
instruments.text: A six-voice desktop chip synth built around two AY-3 sound chips, with a 16-step sequencer.

instruments.name: UDO Audio Super 6
instruments.text: A twelve-voice binaural analogue-hybrid polysynth whose FPGA digital oscillators feed a true-stereo analogue signal path, later also sold as a keyboardless desktop version.

instruments.name: UDO Audio Super Gemini
instruments.text: A 20-voice bi-timbral analogue-hybrid flagship with FPGA oscillators, analogue low-pass filters, a stereo signal path, a five-octave polyphonic-aftertouch keyboard and a ribbon controller.

instruments.name: Vermona MARS
instruments.text: A monophonic analogue synth that preceded the Perfourmer in Vermona's modern range.

instruments.name: Vermona Perfourmer
instruments.text: A five-rack-space analogue synthesizer with four voices and 74 front-panel controls, later revised as the Perfourmer MkII.

instruments.name: Vermona Mono Lancet
instruments.text: A desktop analogue monosynth with two VCOs, a 24dB low-pass filter, one ADSR and an LFO, later updated as the Mono Lancet '15.

instruments.name: Waldorf Microwave
instruments.text: Waldorf's first synthesiser, a rack-mounted wavetable synthesiser developed from the PPG Wave.

instruments.name: Waldorf Wave
instruments.text: A wavetable keyboard synthesiser with 16 voices as standard, expandable to 32 or 48.

instruments.name: Waldorf Pulse
instruments.text: A monophonic analogue rack synthesiser, revised in 1997 as the Pulse+ with an added audio input and a MIDI/CV/gate interface.

instruments.name: Waldorf Microwave II
instruments.text: A wavetable rack synthesiser driven by a Motorola DSP.

instruments.name: Waldorf Microwave XT
instruments.text: A Microwave II wavetable synthesiser with 44 knobs and an audio input in a 5U package.

instruments.name: Waldorf Microwave XTk
instruments.text: The Microwave XT wavetable synthesiser with a 49-key keyboard.

instruments.name: Waldorf Q
instruments.text: A DSP-driven virtual analogue synthesiser with 58 knobs, also sold as the Q Rack and, from 2002, as the red Q+ with up to 100 voices and 16 analogue low-pass filters.

instruments.name: Waldorf microQ
instruments.text: A compact virtual analogue synthesiser with 25 voices, upgradable to 75, later also sold as the microQ Keyboard.

instruments.name: Waldorf Blofeld
instruments.text: An affordable desktop module combining the sound engines of the Q and the Microwave, later also sold as the Blofeld Keyboard.

instruments.name: Waldorf Pulse 2
instruments.text: A paraphonic analogue desktop synthesiser, the successor to the Pulse.

instruments.name: Waldorf Rocket
instruments.text: A small paraphonic hybrid desktop synthesiser.

instruments.name: Waldorf Streichfett
instruments.text: A desktop string synthesiser.

instruments.name: Waldorf Quantum
instruments.text: Waldorf's flagship analogue/digital hybrid keyboard synthesiser.

instruments.name: Waldorf Kyra
instruments.text: A 128-voice virtual analogue module described as the first synthesiser to run entirely on an FPGA.

instruments.name: Waldorf STVC
instruments.text: A keyboard version of the Streichfett string synthesiser with an added vocoder.

instruments.name: Waldorf Iridium
instruments.text: A digital 16-voice, dual-timbral polyphonic desktop module, later also sold as the Iridium Keyboard.

instruments.name: Waldorf M
instruments.text: A hybrid 8-voice polyphonic desktop module with two digital wavetable oscillators per voice.

instruments.name: Waldorf Iridium Core
instruments.text: A compact 12-voice desktop carrying the full Iridium engine, with wavetable, multi-sample and granular, waveform, resonator and kernel FM synthesis and dual digital filters.

instruments.name: Waldorf Quantum MK2
instruments.text: A new version of the Quantum hybrid synthesiser with a keyboard capable of polyphonic aftertouch among other changes.

instruments.name: Waldorf Protein
instruments.text: A compact 8-voice desktop wavetable synthesiser built around the original Microwave 1 ASIC oscillators, with up to four layers, an arpeggiator, step sequencer and effects.

instruments.name: Waldorf Iridium Desktop MK2
instruments.text: A 16-voice second generation of the Iridium desktop with a faster CPU board, more RAM and flash storage, up to four layers, a new Seeds synthesis method and per-note parameter locks.

instruments.name: Yamaha SY-1
instruments.text: Yamaha's first synthesiser, an analogue monosynth with a 37-key keyboard derived from the solo section of the GX-707 Electone prototype, with initial and after touch.

instruments.name: Yamaha GX-1
instruments.text: A concert-model Electone and Yamaha's first polyphonic synthesiser, an analogue console with two 61-key eight-voice manuals of two oscillators per voice, a monophonic solo keyboard with a ribbon, and a pedalboard, used by Keith Emerson and Stevie Wonder.

instruments.name: Yamaha SY-2
instruments.text: The successor to the SY-1, an analogue monosynth built largely around presets, with high-pass and low-pass filters.

instruments.name: Yamaha CS-10
instruments.text: An analogue monosynth with a single oscillator, a noise generator, one multimode filter and two envelopes.

instruments.name: Yamaha CS-30
instruments.text: The top of Yamaha's original analogue monosynth range, with two VCOs, two multimode filters, two VCAs, three envelope generators, a ring modulator, switchable signal routing and an eight-step analogue sequencer.

instruments.name: Yamaha CS-30L
instruments.text: A live-performance version of the CS-30 analogue monosynth without its step sequencer, built into a tolex case with chrome legs.

instruments.name: Yamaha CS-50
instruments.text: A four-voice analogue polysynth in the CS series, with a simpler architecture than the CS-80.

instruments.name: Yamaha CS-60
instruments.text: An eight-voice analogue polysynth with one oscillator per voice, a resonant high-pass and low-pass filter and a 61-key keyboard, a smaller and cheaper version of the CS-80 without its polyphonic aftertouch.

instruments.name: Yamaha CS-15
instruments.text: An analogue monosynth with two VCOs, two 12 dB multimode filters, two ADSR envelopes, an LFO and flexible routing on a 37-key keyboard, used by the Human League on Dare.

instruments.name: Yamaha CS-5
instruments.text: A low-priced analogue monosynth with one VCO, one multimode filter, one envelope and an LFO with sample and hold, on a 37-key keyboard.

instruments.name: Yamaha CS-15D
instruments.text: A dual-channel analogue monosynth with presets and a 37-key keyboard, a different design from the CS-15, whose pitch-bend and modulation wheels Yamaha still uses.

instruments.name: Yamaha CS-20M
instruments.text: An analogue monosynth on a 37-key keyboard that used digital technology to store its sounds in patch memories.

instruments.name: Yamaha CS-40M
instruments.text: A duophonic analogue synthesiser with patch memory, a multimode filter and a 44-key keyboard.

instruments.name: Yamaha CS-70M
instruments.text: A six-voice dual-channel analogue polysynth with patch memories, an auto-tune function and a microprocessor-driven polyphonic sequencer, on a 61-key keyboard.

instruments.name: Yamaha GS1
instruments.text: Yamaha's first FM synthesiser keyboard, built for stage use with touch control and magnetic voice cards, heard throughout Toto's fourth album.

instruments.name: Yamaha GS2
instruments.text: A 16-voice FM synthesiser with a 73-key keyboard, sold beside the GS1.

instruments.name: Yamaha CS01
instruments.text: A battery-powered analogue monosynth with one VCO and one filter, a 32-key mini keyboard, a built-in speaker, a breath-controller input and strap pins, later revised as the CS01 II.

instruments.name: Yamaha DX1
instruments.text: The top DX-series FM synthesiser, with two DX7 tone generators for 32 voices, single, dual or split modes, and a 73-key weighted keyboard with polyphonic aftertouch in a rosewood case.

instruments.name: Yamaha DX9
instruments.text: A 16-voice FM synthesiser in the DX7 family with four operators instead of six, eight algorithms, 20 memory locations and a 61-key keyboard.

instruments.name: Yamaha TX816
instruments.text: A rack FM tone generator system holding eight DX7 tone generator modules, each with its own output, for layering or multi-part use from MIDI.

instruments.name: Yamaha DX21
instruments.text: An eight-voice, bi-timbral four-operator FM synthesiser with eight algorithms, 128 presets, split and dual modes, a chorus and a 61-key keyboard without velocity.

instruments.name: Yamaha DX27
instruments.text: An eight-voice four-operator FM synthesiser, a full-size-key version of the DX100 with 192 presets and 61 keys without velocity, also sold with speakers as the DX27S.

instruments.name: Yamaha DX5
instruments.text: An FM synthesiser with two DX7 tone generators for 32 voices and a 76-key keyboard.

instruments.name: Yamaha TX7
instruments.text: A desktop module version of the DX7 FM tone generator, positioned as an expansion for layering DX7 voices, with a cassette interface for voice storage.

instruments.name: Yamaha DX7II
instruments.text: The second-generation DX7, a 16-voice six-operator FM synthesiser with dual tone generators for bi-timbral layers and splits, stereo output and an aluminium case, sold as the DX7IID and as the DX7IIFD with a floppy drive.

instruments.name: Yamaha FB-01
instruments.text: A compact eight-voice, eight-part multitimbral four-operator FM sound module, a forerunner of the TG and MU series.

instruments.name: Yamaha DX11
instruments.text: An eight-voice four-operator FM synthesiser with a 61-key keyboard, the keyboard version of the TX81Z, sold in Japan as the V2.

instruments.name: Yamaha DX7S
instruments.text: A lower-priced six-operator FM synthesiser released beside the DX7II in the same case, playing a single voice in mono without its layering and stereo features.

instruments.name: Yamaha TX802
instruments.text: The DX7II's 16-voice six-operator FM tone generator in a 2U rack module.

instruments.name: Yamaha DS55
instruments.text: A low-cost eight-voice four-operator FM synthesiser with a 61-key keyboard, meant as a link between Yamaha's home keyboards and its professional range.

instruments.name: Yamaha TQ5
instruments.text: A desktop eight-voice four-operator FM tone generator with eight algorithms, the module equivalent of the YS200.

instruments.name: Yamaha YS100
instruments.text: An eight-voice four-operator FM synthesiser with a 61-key keyboard, a version of the YS200 without its sequencer and aftertouch.

instruments.name: Yamaha YS200
instruments.text: An eight-voice, eight-part four-operator FM synthesiser with an eight-track sequencer, a rhythm section, reverb, delay and distortion effects and a 61-key keyboard.

instruments.name: Yamaha SY77
instruments.text: A 16-part multitimbral workstation combining AFM synthesis and AWM2 sample playback (RCM synthesis) with resonant digital filters, effects, a sequencer and a 61-key keyboard with aftertouch.

instruments.name: Yamaha TG55
instruments.text: A 1U rack AWM2 sample-playback tone generator with 16-note polyphony, the module version of the SY55.

instruments.name: Yamaha V50
instruments.text: A music workstation combining a 16-voice, eight-part four-operator FM engine equivalent to two TX81Z modules with an eight-track sequencer, a PCM rhythm machine, effects and a 61-key keyboard.

instruments.name: Yamaha SY22
instruments.text: A 16-note vector synthesiser combining AWM sample and two-operator FM elements under a joystick and vector envelopes, with a 61-key keyboard with aftertouch.

instruments.name: Yamaha SY55
instruments.text: A 16-note AWM2 sample-based synthesiser that layers up to four sampled-wave elements per voice, with effects and a 61-key keyboard.

instruments.name: Yamaha TG33
instruments.text: A desktop 16-note AWM and FM vector tone generator with a joystick, the module version of the SY22.

instruments.name: Yamaha TG77
instruments.text: The 3U rack version of the SY77, with its RCM combination of AFM and AWM2 synthesis, resonant filters and eight individual outputs.

instruments.name: Yamaha SY99
instruments.text: A workstation combining six-operator AFM synthesis and AWM2 sample playback that can load external samples, with a sequencer and a 76-key keyboard.

instruments.name: Yamaha SY35
instruments.text: A 16-note AWM and FM vector synthesiser on the SY22's design, with 16-bit samples and a 61-key keyboard.

instruments.name: Yamaha SY85
instruments.text: A 30-voice AWM2 sample-based workstation without FM, with sample RAM, eight sliders, a nine-track sequencer, a floppy drive and a 61-key keyboard with aftertouch.

instruments.name: Yamaha TG500
instruments.text: A 1U rack AWM2 sample-playback tone generator with 64-note polyphony, the module version of the SY85.

instruments.name: Yamaha VL1
instruments.text: The first synthesiser with Yamaha's Virtual Acoustic physical-modelling tone generation, simulating wind and string instruments with two-note polyphony on a 49-key keyboard.

instruments.name: Yamaha VL1m
instruments.text: The module version of the VL1 Virtual Acoustic physical-modelling synthesiser.

instruments.name: Yamaha VL7
instruments.text: A monophonic, lower-cost version of the VL1 Virtual Acoustic physical-modelling synthesiser, with a 49-key keyboard.

instruments.name: Yamaha VP1
instruments.text: A 16-voice Virtual Acoustic physical-modelling synthesiser using free-oscillation F/VA synthesis rather than the VL1's self-oscillation type.

instruments.name: Yamaha W5
instruments.text: A 32-voice AWM2 workstation with 8 MB of wave memory, six effect processors, 16-part multitimbrality, GM support and a 76-key keyboard.

instruments.name: Yamaha W7
instruments.text: A 32-voice AWM2 workstation with 8 MB of wave memory, six effect processors, 16-part multitimbrality, GM support and a 61-key keyboard.

instruments.name: Yamaha QS300
instruments.text: A 32-voice AWM2 music workstation supporting the XG format, with a sequencer and a 61-key keyboard.

instruments.name: Yamaha CS1x
instruments.text: A 32-voice AWM2 sample-based Control Synthesizer aimed at dance musicians, with six sound-control knobs, an early built-in arpeggiator, XG voices and a 61-key keyboard.

instruments.name: Yamaha VL70-m
instruments.text: A compact monophonic Virtual Acoustic physical-modelling tone generator, a lower-cost version of the VL1m.

instruments.name: Yamaha AN1x
instruments.text: Yamaha's first virtual analogue synthesiser, a ten-voice DSP analogue-physical-modelling instrument with two oscillators per voice, two scenes per patch, a ribbon controller and a 61-key keyboard.

instruments.name: Yamaha CS2x
instruments.text: The successor to the CS1x, a 64-note AWM2 sample-based Control Synthesizer with a larger sample ROM, 24 dB filters, 16 parts in Multi mode and a 61-key keyboard.

instruments.name: Yamaha EX5
